title: Deep Learning-Based Real-Time Sign Language Translation System for Telehealth Applications
abstract: Every human being requires communication; however, people with hearing and speech disabilities have difficulty conveying messages, particularly in urgent and professional settings like the health sector. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based real-time sign language translation system specifically designed for Sri Lanka’s telehealth applications. The system extracts spatial-temporal features with an I3D (Inflated 3D ConvNet) and tests three sequence-to-sequence models: T5, LSTM, and Transformer decoders. Out of the three evaluated models in the paper, the Encoder-Transformer-Decoder performed the best relative to the other models evaluated. To allow instant interaction for both patients and professionals, a real-time bi-directional desktop application using socket communication was implemented. The system’s main focus is prompt interaction with an emphasis on Sri Lanka’s telehealth translation demands, providing high-speed translation, accessibility, and accuracy at the sentence level. The work demonstrates some promise, but the remaining issues of the lack of sufficient datasets and the need for localization of the language still pose problems. As a result, integrating multiple languages and modalities and improving the real-world usefulness and the quality of the translation of the system remain the focus of future work.

title: LSTM based Model for Weather-based Solar Irradiance Prediction for Long-Term PV Energy Planning
abstract: The increasing global emphasis on sustainable energy solutions has elevated the role of solar power as a prominent renewable energy source. Photovoltaic (PV) systems face the challenge of the presence of an uncertainty in long-term energy production due to the stochastic and intermittent nature of solar irradiance. Accurate forecasting of solar irradiance is essential for planning and optimizing PV plant performance. Traditionally, long-term solar irradiance forecasting relies on historical irradiance data. However, such data is often limited to short durations (2–5 years) at prospective PV plant sites, whereas reliable forecasts may require 15 or more years of data. To address this limitation, we propose a novel deep learning-based methodology that leverages Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks enhanced with attention mechanisms to reconstruct historical solar irradiance using available long-term meteorological data. This approach exploits the known correlation between weather parameters and solar irradiance, filling in historical data gaps and enabling long-term forecasting. The proposed model predicts missing irradiance values and also facilitates extended solar energy generation forecasts essential for site planning and investment decisions. A case study is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the model, and the proposed model achieved an RMSE of 66.9 W/m2and R2= 0.9578 for Colombo and 56.7 W/m2, R2= 0.9683 for Hotevilla, outperforming the conventional LSTM by approximately 3-5%. Hence, this study contributes to the growing body of research in solar forecasting by offering a practical and accurate solution for long-term irradiance prediction using limited observed data.

title: Computer Vision-Based Remote Monitoring System for Phenotyping and Analysis of Tea
abstract: This study introduces a computer vision-based continuous remote monitoring system for plant phenotyping and crop condition assessment in perennial crops, with a focus on a tea plantation under dynamic outdoor conditions. The system integrates hardware for continuous data acquisition, including environmental sensors to measure temperature, humidity, and irradiance, alongside high-resolution cameras for visual monitoring. To address limitations in traditional manual phenotyping methods, we formulated a dataset through image annotation and augmentation, and trained a U-Net model for semantic segmentation of tea shoots and canopy, evaluated using Dice score, precision, recall, and F1score metrics. Analysis of derived parameters, such as Shoot Area Ratio (SAR), Canopy Area Ratio (CAR), and Daily Light Integral (DLI), revealed temporal variations in plant growth and correlations with environmental factors such as temperature. Clustering techniques further distinguished optimal growth conditions from suboptimal ones. The approach demonstrates the potential of automated systems to enhance understanding of crop-environment interactions, supporting sustainable management of tea plantations.

title: Environment-Aware Intention Generation in Robots via Multistage Perception and Language Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a real-time framework for generating humanoid intent designed for service-oriented robots operating across diverse environments. The system integrates visual perception, environment classification, and a hybrid large language model (LLM) reasoning to enable context-aware, human-like behavior. A YOLOv8x-based perception module detects 43 object classes with a mAP@0.5 of 0.89. In contrast, object distributions are processed by a lightweight artificial neural network (ANN) that classifies environments with high accuracy (≈99.4%) and near-perfect F1-scores across all classes. A hybrid LLM mechanism governs reasoning. When ANN confidence is high, Groq’s Llama 3.3 70B model provides rapid, low-latency (~36.3ms) intent generation; when confidence is low, OpenAI GPT-4o is invoked for vision-based inference and richer semantic reasoning. The framework operates on a cloud-edge deployment, with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) handling inference and a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B capturing live video streams. A Flask-based web interface visualizes object detections, environment predictions, and generates intentions with real-time audio-visual feedback. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s ability to maintain real-time performance while producing contextually appropriate, socially aligned responses, establishing its potential for adaptive and assistive humanoid robotic applications.

title: Detection and Correction of Misspelled Content in Transcribed Sinhala
abstract: Accurate transcription of spoken Sinhala language into written form is a complex task that is influenced by numerous challenges, such as speech recognition errors, phonetic variations, and typographical inconsistencies. This paper presents a detailed methodology for detecting and correcting misspelled words within transcribed Sinhala text. The proposed system integrates tokenization, stemming, NGram similarity matching, diacritic mark (pillam) removal, and normalization, as well as KenLM-based language model scoring to improve linguistic accuracy. Specifically, the proposed system incorporates pillam removal and normalization to enhance the accuracy of misspelled word correction beyond existing approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that this multi-stage approach effectively improves the fluency and contextual appropriateness of corrected sentences, thereby offering significant improvements for natural language processing applications in Sinhala. The approach achieved recall scores of 70.34% and 53.91% for misspelled word detection and correction respectively.

title: FlowSegModel: Advancing Perception in Autonomous Driving Through Weather-Resilient Segmentation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodology for semantic segmentation in adverse weather conditions, employing a FlowSegModel architecture that integrates RGB images with optical flow inputs within a modified DeepLabV3 framework, evaluated on the VKITTI2 dataset. The FlowSegModel adapts the DeepLabV3 backbone, by reconfiguring its initial convolutional layer to accommodate a 5-channel input (3 RGB + 2 optical flow), enabling fusion of spatial and motion features. This is complemented by a tailored Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module, optimized with adjusted dilation rates to capture multi-scale context under degraded visibility. The proposed FlowSegModel achieves mean Intersection over Union (IoU) scores of 0.8406 under normal conditions and 0.8034 in adverse scenarios (fog, rain, overcast), demonstrating a robust 4.4% degradation. This resilience is attributed to optical flow’s complementary motion cues, enhancing visibility in degraded environments. Comparative analyses reveal that fine-tuned SEARAFT and RAFT models outperform classical methods (e.g., Farneback, Horn-Schunck) by over 96% in Average End-Point Error (EPE) reduction, with SEA-RAFT excelling by 56.6% over RAFT. An ablation study confirms the superiority of RGB-flow fusion, yielding a 46.1% mean IoU improvement over an optical-flow-only variant, which struggles with static scene discrimination absent color and texture data. These findings hold significant implications for autonomous driving and outdoor vision systems, offering a practical approach to weather-invariant perception that may reduce real-world failure rates. This work advances robust segmentation techniques, contributing to safer and more reliable environmental perception in challenging conditions.

title: End-to-End Deep Learning for Lane Keeping Assist on Unmarked Sri Lankan Roads
abstract: Lane Keeping Assist (LKA) systems are critical for enhancing road safety by preventing unintentional lane departures. Conventional LKA approaches rely primarily on lane markings, limiting their effectiveness on roads with inconsistent or faded markings, such as those commonly found in developing countries. This paper presents an end-to-end deep learning approach using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict steering angles directly from camera inputs, eliminating the need for explicit lane detection or hand-engineered features. The model is trained on a dataset collected from local Sri Lankan roads, incorporating data augmentation to improve robustness under varied lighting and road conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the capability of the proposed system to learn lane-keeping behavior with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.1754, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.2522, and R2Score of 0.3509, highlighting its potential for enhancing safety in challenging driving environments. Building on the trained CNN, we introduce a framework that pairs primary human input with secondary CNN predictions. We demonstrate that disagreements between these two sources, without requiring insight into their internal mechanisms, can be exploited to enhance decision accuracy. Furthermore, we define a disagreement threshold such that when the divergence between human and CNN predictions exceeds this value, the driver is issued life-critical alerts.

title: Feature Conditioned Diffusion for Audio Generation
abstract: Audio generation has taken a leap forward with tools that recreate sounds using spectral data, like spectrograms. State of the art audio generation with diffusion models is typically conditioned only on Mel spectrograms. We explored a new approach using the DiffWave model with conditioning features such as Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Constant Q Transform (CQT), Karhunen-Loève Transform (KLT), and their combinations, tested on LJSpeech, ESC-50, and IRMAS datasets for speech, environmental, and music synthesis. Among the tested methods, the combination of Mel spectrogram and CQT spectrogram achieved the lowest Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) scores (5.45 on LJSpeech, 6.71 on ESC-50, 4.60 on IRMAS) while maintaining strong precision and coverage. Our results demonstrate that this technique significantly outperforms conventional conditioning methods, offering a promising new approach for audio generation.

title: A Lightweight Modular Pipeline for Edge-Optimized Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight, modular deep learning pipeline for real-time plant disease detection, optimized for edge devices. To balance accuracy, model size, and inference speed, we employ YOLOv8n and YOLOv8n-seg for leaf detection and segmentation, achieving mAP@0.5 scores of 63.2% and 99.5% pixel accuracy, respectively. The segmentation model is trained on pre-separated leaf images, allowing accurate boundary detection.For classification, MobileNetV3-Small with 976K parameters is used, reaching 89.81% accuracy across five turmeric leaf disease classes. Through structured pruning of convolutional and dense layers—while retaining normalization and activation layers—the parameter count is reduced by 50% (488K), with minimal accuracy loss.To handle partial occlusion, a lightweight U-Net-based GAN module (177K parameters) reconstructs missing leaf regions, improving classification reliability. The pipeline is designed for deployment on NVIDIA Jetson Nano, using post-training quantization (FP16, INT8) for faster inference, with FP32 fallback when needed.The modular structure allows independent optimization of components, ensuring computational efficiency. This design makes the pipeline suitable for scalable, real-time agricultural applications, especially in resource-constrained environments, supporting precision farming through reliable and efficient disease monitoring

title: Application on basic life support and first aid
abstract: Medical emergencies such as trauma, poisoning, burns, drowning and asthma exacerbations account for a major proportion of preventable deaths in Sri Lanka, where delays in pre-hospital intervention are common. Despite high smartphone penetration, existing first aid apps are predominantly foreign, English-only, and not aligned with Sri Lankan emergency patterns or healthcare pathways. This project aimed to develop a localized mobile application that provides real-time first aid and Basic Life Support (BLS) guidance to bridge the critical gap between emergency onset and hospital care. A comprehensive literature review was conducted on current first aid mobile applications, gaps in public knowledge, and emergency trends in Sri Lanka. Ten common emergencies were identified, and algorithm-based first aid flows were designed according to WHO Integrated Management of Adolescent and Adult Illness (IMAI) guidelines. A prototype app was developed with three user modes — caregiver, paramedic, and administrator - integrating multilingual (Sinhala, Tamil, English) text, voice and AI-assisted visual guidance, GPS hospital navigation, quiz-based learning, and live doctor connectivity. The application enables laypersons to manage burns, animal bites, trauma, choking, asthma and other emergencies through instant voice/visual instructions while simultaneously contacting ambulances or hospitals via GPS. Administrators can update medical content, while paramedics receive real-time emergency alerts with guided navigation to patients. The app also tracks user engagement with emergencies and learning modules. This prototype demonstrates the feasibility of a context-aware, multilingual, interactive digital solution to improve emergency response capacity in Sri Lanka. By empowering bystanders during the pre-hospital phase, the app has the potential to reduce morbidity and mortality while strengthening community-level preparedness. Future development will focus on enhancing AI accuracy, offline use and national emergency system integration

title: UltraLight+: An Optimized Progressive CNN Architecture for Efficient Image Classification
abstract: This paper presents UltraLight+, a novel progressive resizing convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture specifically designed for resource-constrained edge devices. Our approach combines dynamic resolution scaling with multi-phase training and introduces hybrid depthwise-separable convolution blocks with adaptive feature fusion mechanisms. UltraLight+ achieves 79.6% accuracy on CIFAR-10 with only 75,530 parameters, representing an 82% parameter reduction compared to MobileNetV2 (0.35α) while delivering 79% higher accuracy (44.4% vs 79.6%). The progressive training protocol, which transitions from 64×64 to 96×96 resolution, enables faster convergence and maintains efficient deployment with a 1.05MB model size. Quantization optimizations achieve 2.1× speedup with minimal accuracy loss (<0.2%), demonstrating practical viability for real-time edge applications.

title: Privacy-Preserving Heart Disease Prediction Using TabTransformer-Based Federated Learning on Non-IID Clinical Data
abstract: Heart disease remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, and accurate early prediction is critical for timely clinical intervention. Traditional machine learning and deep learning approaches often rely on centralised patient data, raising significant concerns regarding privacy, security, and regulatory compliance. In this study, the researcher proposes a privacy-preserving federated learning framework that integrates a TabTransformer architecture with the FedProx optimisation algorithm to predict heart disease from tabular clinical data. The framework is specifically designed to address non-identically distributed (non-IID) client data across multiple healthcare institutions, ensuring stable model convergence while preserving data confidentiality. A privacy-preserving protocol and interpretability analysis further highlight its practicality for real-world deployments.

title: Explainable and Robust Detection of AI Bot-Generated Social Dialogues Using a Hybrid Feature-Attention Framework
abstract: This research paper aims to address significant challenges posed by rapidly evolving conversational AI bots in distinguishing them from genuine humans in social dialogs. Traditional detection methods relying on static patterns or simple heuristics fall short against advanced adaptive bots. A novel hybrid approach is proposed, which combines deep explainability and adversarial robustness to effectively detect conversational bots. The method employs meticulous data preprocessing, extracting numeric features and semantic BERT embeddings processed through a dual-branch neural network enhanced with attention mechanisms. Adversarial training through embedding perturbations strengthens robustness against subtle textual manipulations, while interpretability is ensured through attention-based insights and SHAP analysis, which led it to create transparent decision rules. The experimental results demonstrate approximately ninety-six percent accuracy, significantly outperforming existing methods. This hybrid framework uniquely balances explainability, robustness, scalability, real-time capabilities, and advanced bot detection in dynamic conversational environments.

title: Hybrid Sensing Approach for Real-Time Chat Behavior Detection and Classify Social Engineered Attacks
abstract: Social engineering attacks in real-time chat environments exploit psychological manipulation to extract sensitive information, posing significant risks to individuals and organizations. Traditional detection methods often struggle with high latency, limited contextual awareness, and poor interpretability, rendering them inadequate for dynamic conversational settings. This paper proposes a novel hybrid system integrating lightweight rule-based pattern matching with machine learning, leveraging DistilBERT embeddings and engineered features for accurate, low-latency detection of social engineering attacks. A rolling fraud score mechanism captures multi-turn conversational threats, while a non-recursive architecture ensures memory efficiency. The proposed method has been evaluated using a composite of real and semi-synthetic multi-turn chat datasets, the hybrid model achieved consistent message and conversation-level performance with $\tilde 93\% $ accuracy and low latency (<500ms), outperforming existing methods in both precision and real-time applicability.

title: Hybrid Transformer-LSTM Autoencoder for Student Final Grade Prediction
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid Transformer-LSTM autoencoder for student final grade prediction, addressing the limitations of existing models that capture either short-term or long-term learning patterns but not both. The model leverages the Transformer’s ability to extract long-range dependencies and LSTM’s strength in modeling sequential short-term behavior, enabling a comprehensive representation of student learning trajectories. Using the Open University Learning Analytics dataset, the approach integrates anomaly detection via reconstruction error to proactively flag at-risk students. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid model outperforms LSTM-only and Transformer-only baselines, achieving an F1-score of 0.85 and an AUC-ROC of 0.92, thereby offering a more reliable framework for early intervention. This contribution highlights both the methodological novelty and the practical utility of the hybrid architecture in educational data mining, making the approach a promising tool for supporting timely and personalized student interventions.

title: Forecasting Solar Power: Enhancing Energy Predictions with LSTM Networks
abstract: The renewable energy sector is experiencing rapid growth, and within this thriving industry, accurate solar power forecasting serves an important function in maintaining efficient energy utilization and reliable grid integration. Moreover, it offers significant economic benefits, contributing to cost savings and enhancing energy distribution efficiency. This paper demonstrates the use of LSTM models to estimate solar plant energy output using sensor-based irradiance data collected through a pyranometer. The LSTM models were trained based on historical data, including time, irradiance, and power output, to forecast future power generation for a solar plant in Vavuniya, Sri Lanka. The dataset covered a one-year period from March 2023 to March 2024. The study shows that the developed models are capable of identifying both long- and short-term dynamics of solar energy generation, making them valuable for forecasting and supporting industries to renewable power systems.

title: Trends of online presence and Artificial Intelligence usage in scholarly publications: A case study based on the University of Colombo, Sri Lanka
abstract: The rapid growth of digital platforms and Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping how scholarly communication is produced, shared, and evaluated. Academic conferences, a key channel for disseminating new knowledge, increasingly rely on institutional repositories and online platforms to make research outputs visible to a broader audience. At the same time, AI tools are becoming embedded in academic writing, raising opportunities and concerns. Against this backdrop, the present study investigates the trends in online availability of conference abstracts and examines the extent of AI usage in their preparation, drawing on five years of conference data from the University of Colombo (UOC). This study aimed to: (a) examine the trends in uploading research abstracts to online platforms and institutional repositories, and (b) explore the use of AI in abstract writing. Proceedings of the annual research conferences of the university from 2020 to 2024 were used as the primary dataset. A quantitative approach was adopted, with Turnitin (TII) employed to check online presence and to identify AI usage. One thousand six hundred ninety-five abstracts have been published across the five years, with the highest number published in 2020 (381) and the lowest in 2022 (285). Average online presence increased from 20.59% in 2020 to over 98% in 2021–2023, though it dropped to 55.07% in 2024, possibly due to an Institutional Repository (IR) malfunction, indicating that many abstracts were not uploaded to the IR or other platforms, limiting plagiarism detection through TII. Average AI usage in abstracts rose steadily, from 0.13% (2020) to 0.41% (2022), 4.44% (2023), and 14.24% (2024). Except for 2021, this reflects a growing reliance on AI tools in academic writing. The findings highlight the importance of increasing the presence of research outputs on academic platforms to detect plagiarism, which will also enhance global accessibility, improve citation rates, and strengthen both researcher h-indexes and university rankings. However, while wider visibility aids plagiarism detection, it does not fully safeguard copyright. The rising use of AI underscores the need for clear policies and training in ethical AI-assisted writing. Properly harnessed, AI can improve quality and support publication in high-impact journals, contributing to the university's academic integrity. Future studies could expand to other universities and publication types for comprehensive findings. The librarians are responsible for initiating and supporting policy development and implementation, as well as raising awareness of these aspects.

title: Social science undergraduates' perceptions of generative Artificial Intelligence tools: A case study
abstract: The penetration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionising the education landscape. To develop a sustainable framework for the use of AI in higher education, it is vital to identify the perception of undergraduates on AI tools. Although a few studies have examined the undergraduate use of AI for academic work in the Sri Lankan context, there is a gap in research in identifying social science undergraduates’ perceptions. Therefore, this study aims to identify the types and purposes of using AI tools, determine undergraduate perception, and find out the relationships between user context and perception of use of AI tools. A survey was conducted with the undergraduates (n=3104) of the Faculty of Arts, University of Colombo, by using the stratified sampling technique based on the academic years with a sample size of 341. A questionnaire was administered to collect data, and 57.4% responded. Data were analysed using SPSS Version 22. Most respondents are between 20-24 years of age (94%), and 87% are females. Respondents use 14 different AI tools, with a majority using a free version of ChatGPT (94%). Most of the respondents (84%) use AI tools daily and smartphones were the preferred devices. Knowledge discovery (65%) is the main purpose of using AI tools, whereas creative work (42%) and assisting in assignments (42%) are the other key purposes. Only 51.2% of undergraduates were satisfied with the use of AI tools, while 38.6% have indicated neutral satisfaction. Ease of use was the main reason to use AI tools, whereas quick response, generation of new ideas and efficiency were the other reasons. Age has a significant relationship with user perception on creativity (p = 0.023) and new idea generation (p = 0.021). Furthermore, significant relationships were observed between the undergraduate perception with subject streams and the level of study. This study concludes that the social science undergraduates of the University of Colombo use different AI tools, and the majority are satisfied with using AI for academic activities. Higher education institutes should consider developing AI policies to align with the changing needs of the undergraduates in the contemporary education landscape.

title: Real-Time Vehicle Classification and Directional Counting at Urban Roads Using YOLOv11 Under Heterogeneous Traffic Conditions
abstract: Urban roads in developing countries face highly heterogeneous traffic, making manual data collection labour-intensive and error-prone. This study presents a deep learning-based approach for real-time vehicle classification and directional counting using the YOLOv11 framework. A custom dataset of 5,200 locally collected images, encompassing 11 vehicle classes defined by the Road Development Authority of Sri Lanka, was used to train two model variants: YOLOv11 medium and YOLOv11 small. To enable directional flow estimation, the system implements a line-pass-based tracking algorithm that distinguishes between up- and down-traffic streams. The system demonstrated high accuracy for common classes, such as cars (Upstream 98.8% and Downstream 96.8%), motorcycles (Upstream 88.8% and Downstream 97.6%), and three-wheelers (Upstream 85.8% and Downstream 98.4%). However, performance variations in other categories highlight the challenges of occlusion and visual ambiguity in mixed-traffic environments. The findings demonstrate that YOLOv11 models trained on locally representative datasets provide a reliable, scalable, and cost-effective alternative to manual survey methods. This approach provides a disaggregated data source to support traffic signal optimisation, intersection analysis, and urban transport planning under complex heterogeneous traffic conditions.

title: Value at Risk of Stock Market Returns Using a Hidden Markov–LSTM Hybrid Model
abstract: Value at Risk (VaR) remains a central measure for downside market risk and is widely used in regulatory and internal risk management frameworks. Accurate VaR forecasting is challenging because equity returns exhibit volatility clustering, heavy tails, and structural changes associated with shifts between calm and turbulent market conditions. This study proposes a hybrid VaR forecasting framework that combines a Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for latent regime identification with a Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network for conditional volatility forecasting. The model is estimated using daily adjusted closing prices for Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) over 2016 to 2022 with a strict out of sample evaluation, where 2016 to 2019 is used for training and 2020 to 2022 is used for testing. The LSTM predicts a realized volatility proxy computed from rolling return dispersion, while the HMM regime sequence is used as an additional explanatory input to capture regime dependent dynamics. Tail risk is handled by fitting a Student t distribution to standardized residuals from the training period and constructing parametric VaR and Expected Shortfall (ES) forecasts at the 1 percent level. Out of sample backtesting using the Kupiec unconditional coverage test indicates that the observed violation frequency is close to the nominal rate and is not rejected, supporting that regime information combined with nonlinear volatility learning improves VaR calibration for equity returns.

title: A Machine Learning Approach for Predicting the Anxiety Status Among O/L Students: A Case Study from Elpitiya Educational Zone
abstract: In Sri Lanka, anxiety and depression are common among youth. This study examined anxiety among$\mathrm{O} / \mathrm{L}$students in the Elpitiya Educational Zone, aiming to identify influential factors and apply machine learning for early detection. After getting the IOBSL ethical clearance approval using the SCARED child questionnaire and a stratified cluster sampling method, data were collected from 417 students, representing a population of 7,060. The study constructed one main response variable (Anxiety), and five sub-anxiety categories are Panic Disorder, Generalized Anxiety, Social Anxiety, Separation Anxiety, and School Avoidance. Overall,$\mathbf{6 1. 3 \%}$of respondents experienced some level of anxiety, 42.2% with possible anxiety, and 19.1% with specific anxiety. The Random Forest classifier yielded the best performance for predicting anxiety, with an accuracy of 63.33%, an$F 1$-score of 0.6239, a recall of 0.6333, and a precision of 0.6710. For multi-label sub-anxiety classification, a Multioutput Classifier with Random Forest achieved an F1-score of 0.7186 and a Hamming loss of 0.3017. Significant factors influencing anxiety included gender, BMI, screen time, physical activity, sleep duration, parental employment, school type, and academic stress. Notably, female students, those under high academic pressure, and those from smaller schools are more prone to anxiety, while regular exercise and 5-7 hours of sleep help reduce it. The results support the importance of mental well-being through awareness and early intervention.

title: Implementation of a Web-Based Complex Formula Editor
abstract: The difficulty of web-based mathematical formula editing increases because it does not support real-time character editing nor accurate handwriting recognition nor seamless database integration for mathematics. Existing solutions often require users to re-enter entire formulas when making corrections, rely on static input methods, or demand knowledge of LaTeX, limiting accessibility for students, researchers, and engineers. The proposed Web-Based Complex Formula Editor enables users to edit individual characters of the formula in real-time so they can change specific formula sections directly without having to re-enter the entire expression. By integrating AI-powered handwriting recognition and structured format conversion (MathML, LaTeX), the system ensures highly accurate symbol recognition and dynamic expression editing. A modern web technology solution with AI-driven methods helps connect usability with computational efficiency to create a versatile userfriendly tool for typing digital mathematical content.

title: Emotion-Based Classification of TikTok Videos Using CNNs and Hashtag Generation via RAG-Enhanced LLMs
abstract: Emotion recognition, an AI-driven computer vision technology, allows software to read interpersonal expressions through visual clues, and in the context of a rapidly growing short-video platform like TikTok, emotional expression and hashtags created by users offer important insights into human behavior in the real world and within social media interactions. TikTok poses significant challenges to automated analysis because of the uncontrolled lighting, fast motion, varying user actions, and audio-visual noise. To address these complexities, the objective of this study is to propose a hybrid model consisting of a CNN-based emotion recognition system and a Retrieval-Augmented LLM (RAG-LLM)–based emotion sensitive hashtag generation unit. Four major emotion categories namely happiness, sadness, anger, and surprise commonly adopted in prior multimedia-based emotion detection studies were selected, and a total of 4,000 TikTok videos were collected and preprocessed. Then input as frames to three CNN models namely MobileNet, VGGNet, and ResNet. The experimental findings indicate that ResNet recorded the best performance (96% accuracy and high precision, recall, F1score, and minimum error rates). Video transcripts and detected emotions were further ranked by an RAG pipeline with the help of a Sentence Transformer and FAISS video storage to access semantically similar samples to guide three lightweight LLMs, namely DistilGPT-2, GPT-Neo, and FLAN-T5. The comparison of performance based on Precision@k, Recall@k, and F1@k shows that FLAN-T5 generates the most contextually relevant and emotion-consistent hashtags. Altogether, this research paper suggests a unified multimodal framework that interpolates CNN-based emotion recognition with smart RAG-enhanced hashtag generation, which would add to the correct and emotion-sensitive analysis of short videos on social networks.

title: Fine-Tuning SinLlama for Sentiment Analysis in Romanized Sinhala-English Code-Mixed Social Media Text
abstract: Romanized Sinhala-English Code-mixed content dominates on Sri Lankan social media platforms. In this low-resource environment, traditional Machine Learning (ML) models have shown efficacy and robustness for NLP tasks like sentiment analysis. But the potential of current Large Language Models (LLMs) is still largely underexplored. In this study, we explore the performance of SinLlama, a Llama-3-8B model further pre-trained on a large Sinhala corpus, for sentiment analysis on Romanized Sinhala-English text. We evaluate the model performance against traditional Machine Learning baselines. Our experimental results show that the fine-tuned SinLlama model achieves an accuracy of 74.2% outperforming traditional ML baselines and demonstrating superior capability in understanding the semantic nuances of Romanized code-mixed text.

title: Deep Learning Techniques for Differentiating Human-Written and AI-Generated Source Codes
abstract: The rapid growth of AI applications capable of writing or rewriting Java software has posed significant problems to teachers and software development divisions, as they now cannot tell whether the code was actually written by a human or generated by an AI. As a solution for this, the objective of the study is to come up with a robust classifier to recognize AI-generated code in Java. The data sample was balanced, comprising of twenty thousand samples of the GPTGCJ Java dataset, which included both human generated and AI generated programs. Following the preprocessing and preparation of the data, four feature extraction methods were used to represent various properties of the code. These were Abstract Syntax Tree features, token-based features, TF-IDF representations and code embeddings. All of the feature types were subsequently tested with three models: Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and XGBoost. To guarantee sound and reliable results, all twelve models were tested using percentage split and k -fold crossvalidation. Among all combinations that were tried, the CNN model that used code embedding features demonstrated the best accuracy of 94.97% and was the most balanced. The findings demonstrate the need to choose the appropriate feature extraction method and model in the analysis of AI-generated code. The suggested methodology is a practical and efficient way of detecting AI-generated Java code both in the academic and the professional world.

title: Explainable AI-Driven Early Screening of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a multifactorial hormonal disorder characterized by irregular menstrual cycles, infertility, and metabolic complications such as type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Accurate and timely detection of PCOS is critical for early intervention and risk mitigation. This study aims to enhance early PCOS diagnosis using a minimal set of discriminative features and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) for transparent and interpretable predictions. A publicly available dataset obtained from Kaggle was employed. Feature selection was performed using two algorithms: the Boruta algorithm and a hybrid method integrating Mutual Information with Recursive Feature Elimination using a Random Forest classifier (RF). The selected features were evaluated through comprehensive benchmarking across multiple machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) classifiers. SHAP-based XAI techniques were applied to interpret model decisions. Experimental results identified the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier as the optimal model, achieving an accuracy of 0.94, F1-score of 0.94, and ROC-AUC of 0.96. A web-based screening tool was subsequently developed to enable early, interpretable, and actionable assessment of PCOS risk, facilitating timely clinical decision-making and personalized health management. This study underscores the effectiveness of combining minimalfeature predictive modeling with XAI in a practical web-based tool, highlighting its potential to support clinicians and endusers in accurate, transparent, and efficient PCOS risk assessment.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Movie Prediction with Particular Scenes
abstract: Movie discovery using traditional metadata-based systems has its limitations when the user is only able to recall particular scenes of a movie instead of movie titles or genres. Large Language Models (LLMs) have emergent semantic reasoning abilities which may address this “Tip-of-the-Tongue” problem, but how well they perform in scene-to-movie prediction is systematically unexamined. This research performs a thorough benchmark assessment of four leading LLMs, namely, GPT-5, Perplexity Sonar Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash and DeepSeek V3.2 Experimental on scene-to-movie prediction tasks on a curated 30 scene description queries with both unambiguous and ambiguous scenarios. Employing consistent prompt engineering, standard parameter settings, and ranking-based evaluation metrics, the research results show that LLMs are significantly more capable than conventional text retrieval baselines as semantic search engines. GPT-5 and Perplexity Sonar Pro had the best performance - Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) 0.9667 & Precision@1 96.67, Gemini 2.5 Flash and DeepSeek V3.2 had competitive but lower performance metrics. Qualitative error analysis found some common failure modes such as temporal knowledge cutoffs for recent releases (those post-2023), confusing gender and character attributes, and misinterpreting the context. The research sets up evaluation protocols, and proves the potential of LLM-based scene retrieval systems, and confirms the move to transformative movie discovery paradigms.

title_search_text: evaluating large language models for movie prediction with particular scenes
abstract_search_text: movie discovery using traditional metadata-based systems has its limitations when the user is only able to recall particular scenes of a movie instead of movie titles or genres. large language models (llms) have emergent semantic reasoning abilities which may address this “tip-of-the-tongue” problem, but how well they perform in scene-to-movie prediction is systematically unexamined. this research performs a thorough benchmark assessment of four leading llms, namely, gpt-5, perplexity sonar pro, gemini 2.5 flash and deepseek v3.2 experimental on scene-to-movie prediction tasks on a curated 30 scene description queries with both unambiguous and ambiguous scenarios. employing consistent prompt engineering, standard parameter settings, and ranking-based evaluation metrics, the research results show that llms are significantly more capable than conventional text retrieval baselines as semantic search engines. gpt-5 and perplexity sonar pro had the best performance - mean reciprocal rank (mrr) 0.9667 & precision@1 96.67, gemini 2.5 flash and deepseek v3.2 had competitive but lower performance metrics. qualitative error analysis found some common failure modes such as temporal knowledge cutoffs for recent releases (those post-2023), confusing gender and character attributes, and misinterpreting the context. the research sets up evaluation protocols, and proves the potential of llm-based scene retrieval systems, and confirms the move to transformative movie discovery paradigms.

title: A Unified Pipeline for Automated Meeting Documentation Using Speech-to-Text, Abstractive Summarization, and Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Automated meeting documentation requires jointly addressing transcription noise, long-context summarization, and affect interpretation in multi-speaker conversations. This paper investigates an end-to-end pipeline that combines speech-to-text, contextual abstractive summarization, and segment-level sentiment labeling to generate actionable meeting minutes. The system uses Whisper for transcription, a transformer encoder-decoder summarizer (T5) with a long-transcript chunking strategy, and a hybrid sentiment module based on VADER and RoBERTa to improve robustness under conversational language. Performance is evaluated using Word Error Rate (WER) for transcription, ROUGE for summarization quality, and F1-score for sentiment classification, together with qualitative feedback from agile project managers. Results show that the pipeline produces readable transcripts and coherent summaries for multi-party meetings, while sentiment labeling provides useful polarity cues that help reviewers identify tense segments and interpret discussion tone. Expert feedback indicates the outputs support faster post-meeting review and clearer follow-up alignment. The work contributes a deployable unified architecture that operationalizes summarization and sentiment analysis within a single meeting-minutes workflow and highlights concrete constraints-overlapping speech, domain jargon, and subtle affect-that guide future improvements in domain adaptation and emotion-aware meeting analytics.

title: Evaluating Instance Segmentation Techniques in Complex Counting Environments using Ornamental Fish Imagery
abstract: Accurate object counting in complex environments presents numerous challenges in computer vision, primarily due to occlusions, overlapping instances, and indistinct object boundaries. This paper presents a comparative analysis of the performance of three state-of-the-art models: Mask R-CNN, Mask R-CNN with PointRend, and Cascade Mask R-CNN, all of which use instance segmentation for counting. Images of ornamental fish were used to simulate real-world counting difficulties, typified by visually complex, clustered scenes. A custom dataset, comprising 2,992 annotations, was compiled and utilized for both training and validation purposes. The same data and evaluation procedures were used to train and test all three models. Under challenging circumstances, the findings show variations in robustness, segmentation accuracy and boundary quality. Mask R-CNN performed well as a baseline model, and PointRend showed good results in refining object edges; however, it was sensitive to resolution and data variability. Cascade Mask R-CNN consistently outperformed the other two models in handling occlusions and generating instance-level predictions. Based on the results, the cascadebased architecture is best suited for real-world counting applications with intricate object distributions. This study provides fundamental insights into the selection of models, for instance-segmentation tasks across various domains.

title: Knowledge Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Domain-Specific Information Extraction with Glossary-Aided Responses
abstract: Long-standing organizations rely heavily on historical documents rich in domain-specific terminology, yet manual retrieval remains slow and error-prone, while standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often struggle with ambiguous jargon, abbreviations, and evolving terminology. To address these challenges, this paper presents a Knowledge Graph-based RAG framework augmented with a glossary-driven semantic interpretation layer designed to improve the accuracy and efficiency of domain-specific question answering. A usermaintained glossary with fuzzy matching enriches the retrieval context by providing precise definitions alongside knowledge graph triples, enabling the LLM to better interpret specialized terminology. The system was evaluated on publicly available realworld clinical trial protocol and a curated set of 30 domain questions. The system achieves a mean context recall of 0.839 and faithfulness of 0.933, confirming accurate graph-grounded retrieval. Glossary integration improved answer relevancy by 48.4% (0.483 → 0.717), The proposed lightweight, interpretable mechanism significantly enhances domain-specific information extraction and offers a scalable solution for preserving institutional knowledge across regulatory, clinical, and legal archives.

title: Evaluation of an Explainable LLM-Powered Chat-Ops for CI/CD Pipeline Diagnostics and Developer Support
abstract: Modern software delivery relies on Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, yet diagnosing failed jobs still demands intensive manual inspection of logs, configuration files, and environment settings. This study presents an explainable LLM powered ChatOps diagnostic assistant that integrates Google Gemini with Discord and GitHub Actions to automatically detect, analyze, and explain CI/CD pipeline failures. The prototype uses structured prompt engineering to generate human readable diagnostic reports that separate Root Cause, Solution Steps, and Preventive Recommendations, while an explainability layer highlights supporting log evidence and adapts explanations to developer roles. Evaluation combines expert based assessment with semantic benchmarking using Sentence BERT across five representative CI/CD failure scenarios. Six domain experts reported high Readability (4.87) and Usefulness (4.83) on a five-point Likert scale, indicating that the explanations were clear, coherent, and actionable. SBERT based comparison with ground truth solutions yielded an average F1 score of 0.57 and cosine similarity of 0.79, demonstrating moderate semantic alignment. These triangulated findings show that the assistant can provide accurate, comprehensible guidance for CI/CD failure diagnostics, while also revealing the need for better grounding to improve precision and contextual specificity. The work contributes a validated framework for integrating explainable AI into DevOps ChatOps workflows and establishes an empirical basis for LLM driven fault diagnosis in CI/CD environments.

title: InfluesCO: Recommending the Right Sri Lankan YouTube Influencer for Your Marketing Needs
abstract: Influencer marketing is rapidly expanding worldwide, yet data-driven and localised creator recommendation systems remain limited, particularly in regions such as Sri Lanka. This paper introduces InfluesCO, an analytical platform that recommends Sri Lankan YouTube content creators for brand collaborations using large-scale metadata, semantic representations, and multi-modal clustering. The system integrates channellevel and video-level features with multilingual embeddings to capture creator identity and content themes. A clustering pipeline groups creators into coherent content categories, enabling direct influencer recommendations and similar-creator discovery. Experimental results indicate that InfluesCO generates contextually relevant recommendations and well-structured creator clusters, demonstrating its effectiveness as a localised influencer analytics platform. A user study based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) demonstrated strong acceptance of the system among 25 participants, with all TAM hypotheses supported. These findings indicate that InfluesCO is both effective and useraligned, offering a practical decision-support tool for influencer selection in emerging digital markets.

title: Explainable AI-Based Automated Grading of Essay and Multiple-Choice Student Responses Using Embedding-Based Semantic Similarity
abstract: Automated evaluation of student responses is becoming more vital in the digital learning process in large-scale learning setting, especially with the rise of Natural Language Processing (NLP) based educational tools where traditional evaluation method require instructors to manually grade work which is time consuming, subjective and hard to scale. This research introduces a complete AutoGrader framework that evaluates descriptive answers both of essay-type and multiple-choice questions (MCQ) type based on semantic similarity through sentence-embedding. The reference answers and student responses to the context are generated as contextual embeddings with the help of two transformer model all-MPNet-base-v2 and all-MiniLM-L6-v2. After calculating the similarity, the responses with a score higher than a pre-defined threshold value are classified as correct. Most importantly this model integrates the Explainable AI (XAI) techniques like Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to provide trustworthy and transparent grading decisions. Such explanations help instructors to know why an answer has been rated as right or wrong. Strong evaluation performance is demonstrated by the experimental results: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 achieved 96.67% accuracy for MCQ responses and 70% for essays responses, while all-MPNet-base-v2 scored 97.78% accuracy for MCQ responses and 76.67% for essays responses. By combining Semantic similarity and XAI together, the framework yields consistent, fair, and comprehensible grading results with meaningful insights.

title: Seatify: A Real-Time Restaurant/Cafe Occupancy Monitoring System Using CCTV Feed
abstract: Restaurants and cafes often face customer dissatisfaction due to the lack of real-time seat availability information, especially during peak hours or group visits. This study presents Seatify, a real-time cafe and restaurant occupancy monitoring system that uses existing CCTV footage and computer vision techniques to detect seat availability without additional sensors. Seatify detects occupied and available seats real-time, identifies and maps the dynamic seating layouts and then display the most up-to-date visual seating layout to customers in real-time via a web page. Additionally, hourly and weekly demand forecasting analytics are provided to cafe owners. Custom trained YOLOv8x object detection model and ByteTrack were used to track people, chairs and tables. Identifying pose of detected persons is done using YOLOv8x pose estimation model. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach offers accurate seat detection, adapts to dynamic layouts, and provides a cost-effective alternative to hardware-based systems. Finally, Seatify is a comprehensive, AI-powered seating management system that enhances customer experience and optimizes seating efficiency.

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Real-Time Student and Tutor Matching: A Design Science Implementation Through FocusDesk
abstract: The demand for timely, topic-specific academic support is increasing among university students in Sri Lanka, while existing digital learning platforms provide limited mechanisms for real-time, micro-level tutoring. In response, this study adopts a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology to design, implement, and evaluate FocusDesk, a web-based micro-tutoring platform that integrates real-time peer-to-peer interaction with a hybrid recommendation mechanism. The recommendation model combines content-based similarity modeling using TF-IDF with collaborative filtering to support tutor matching under sparse interaction conditions. Experimental evaluation was conducted using a combination of pre-deployment model initialization and interaction data collected during system usage, complemented by a controlled pilot study to assess usability. The results indicate stable matching behavior under early-stage deployment conditions and a positive user experience for short, topic-focused tutoring sessions. This study demonstrates the technical feasibility and practical viability of integrating hybrid machine-learning based matching with real-time micro-tutoring in a resource constrained higher education context. The results highlight the potential of such systems to support timely, topic-focused academic assistance and provide a foundation for future investigations into learning outcomes, fairness-aware recommendation, and scalable peerlearning platforms.

title: Neural Machine Translation in English to Tamil Using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) faces challenges with low-resource language pairs like English-Tamil due to data scarcity and linguistic complexity. This paper investigates enhancing English-to-Tamil translation by efficiently fine-tuning Google's Gemma 3 4B instruction-tuned model. We employed Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), optimized via the Unsloth library, on a 4-bit quantized model. Training was conducted for two epochs on a synthetic English-Tamil dataset (1836 pairs) using the SFTTrainer. Evaluating on a 204-pair test set, our fine-tuned model achieved a BLEU score of 36.12 and a chrF++ score of 65.25. This significantly surpasses the base Gemma 3 4B (BLEU 28.84, chrF++ 59.95) and Llama 3 8B Instruct (BLEU 2.94, chrF++ 21.35) baselines. The results confirm that LoRA-based PEFT, even with synthetic data, provides a resource-efficient and effective method for adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve NMT quality for low-resource languages like Tamil. The fine-tuned model is publicly available.

title: Improving Label Consistency in Tamil Emotion Datasets Through a Multi-Method Relabeling Pipeline
abstract: Emotion classification in Tamil remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-quality annotated datasets and the prevalence of label inconsistencies that undermine model performance. To address this problem, we propose a multi-method relabeling pipeline that combines generative modelling (GPT-4o mini), cross-lingual transfer learning with XLM-RoBERTa, improved deep embedded clustering (BIF-DCN), and a confidence-calibrated ensemble voting strategy to produce more reliable labels for the ACTSEA Tamil emotion corpus. The dataset was first reorganised using an$80 / 20$split with a human-validated test set, after which all relabeling methods were applied exclusively to the training portion. Experimental evaluation using a Support Vector Machine classifier showed that the baseline accuracy of 0.43 increased to 0.52 after relabeling, with substantial gains observed in class-wise F1 scores and a clearer diagonal structure in the confusion matrix, indicating improved separability across emotion categories. The study demonstrates that enhancing dataset quality—rather than model complexity—is key to achieving reliable performance in low-resource settings, and offers a reproducible hybrid framework for noise reduction, label refinement, and cross-lingual adaptation in Tamil and other under-resourced languages.

title: A Two-Stage Deep Learning Method for Detecting Dental Lesions and Predicting Their Severity Levels
abstract: The role of oral health in human health is crucial. As the mouth is exposed to various external inputs, it becomes highly vulnerable to germs, which can cause lesions. Therefore, early detection of such lesions is essential. Diagnosis is commonly carried out through visual examination, radiographs, and biopsy. Although widely used, these methods present challenges: early lesions may be small or resemble healthy tissue, making them difficult to identify. Visual assessments can be subjective, and interpreting radiographs is often time-consuming. This study addresses these limitations by identifying lesions and predicting their severity. The study aims to classify dental images into three lesion categories: Gingivitis, Calculus, and Hypodontia and determine the severity level as mild, moderate, or severe. After data collection, preprocessing and feature extraction were performed. The methodology used RGB dental images and compares the performance of three pre-trained CNN architectures: EfficientNetB0, DenseNet121, and ResNet50. The datasets were trained and tested using multiple data splits, and performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F- score, and error values. DenseNet121 achieved the highest accuracy of$\mathbf{8 6. 9 1 \%}$and showed strong recall across all classes for lesion identification. For severity prediction, DenseNet121 and ResNet50 performed best, demonstrating reliable classification across severity levels. Overall, this study presents a practical deep learning approach for early dental screening using basic front-mouth photographs, making it suitable for potential clinical application. The comparison of multiple CNN models highlights their effectiveness in detecting oral lesions and predicting severity, contributing to AI-based diagnostic support in dentistry.

title: Towards Vision-Based Intersection Navigation: Explainable Insights from Synthetic and Real-World Model Adaptation
abstract: Vision-based navigation offers an infrastructure-free substitute to GPS and external positioning systems, making it a worthy contender for robots operating in indoor environments such as libraries and supermarkets. This work proposes a novel ego-centric vision waypoint based navigation framework by formulating intersection understanding as a multi-label concept learning problem. To ensure a model can be trained with limited data and still preserve the conceptual understanding, each intersection is decomposed into its fundamental directional components: left, right, and forward. Further, we augment the limited real data with synthetic visual data collected from a safer digital twin environment which replicates the real-world scenes. We show that, (i) Model trained using digital twin data alone can yield an F1-score of 0.6 in real-world predictions, compared to 0.5 from a random classifier. (ii) Introducing limited real-world training data can bring the model up to near-perfect accuracy with faster convergence. (iii)The multi-label classification of junctions provides insightful visual explanations ensuring reliability and generalizability of the conceptual framework.

title: Hybrid Deep Learning Feature Extraction with Online Incremental Learning for Robust Stock Price Prediction
abstract: Stock price prediction is a challenging time- Series forecasting problem, which is non-linear, volatile, and subject to concept drift, which influences financial decision-making in the trading, risk management, and portfolio optimization sectors. In this paper, a comparative analysis with evaluation of five deep learning architectures, such as Long Short-Term Memory, Gated Recurrent Unit, CNN-LSTM, Transformer, N-BEATS, and four incremental machine learning models like SGDRegressor, PassiveAggressiveRegressor, Adaptive Random Forest Regressor, Hoeffding Tree Regressor) to predict Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) daily closing prices is presented. An effective feature engineering pipeline with 22 technical indicators, including trend indicators (SMA, EMA, MACD) and momentum indicators (RSI), volatility indicators (Bollinger Bands, ATR), and lagged price indicators, was obtained in addition to stock split adjustment and outlier removal steps. Time-series cross-validation was conducted on 30 unique configurations, and the hyperparameter optimization was fairly addressed to compare the models. The Gated Recurrent Unit model proved to be the best performer, with a test$R^{2} =0.9783$, RMSE$=0.0240$, MAE$=0.0174$and MAPE$=2.16$percent, performing much better than all the other architectures such as traditional LSTM ($R^{2}=0.9271$), Transformer ($R^{2}=0.9081$) and incremental learning model. The results confirm the outstanding performance of gated recurrent-based models in identifying the long-term dependence in financial time series and provide new standards of hybrid deep-incremental learning systems in adaptive stock market forecasting.

title: B+ Indexer: Self-Regulated and Automatic Database Index Maintenance Using Artificial Neural Network
abstract: The conventional approach for database index maintenance includes manual intervention of the database administrator to select time-consuming queries from the organization's database, identify potential indexes for those queries, and maintain them accordingly based on the current workload. This can be time-consuming and overwhelming if the database scale is large. Therefore, the B+ Indexer proposes a solution to automate this process with minimal DBA intervention. Once integrated, it can automatically identify time-consuming queries and recommend appropriate indexes. The B+ Indexer is proactive, meaning that it predicts the next time execution of a particular time-consuming query using a dedicated neural network model trained using past data and creates indexes before the predicted time. In addition, it removes the indexes after the query is executed, thus resolving the problem of update overheads. The B+ Indexer deploys its backend services as set of containerized services using Docker while providing a comprehensive and DBA-friendly desktop application that connects to the target API for performance monitoring and manual configurations. The evaluation strategy and results have shown that the B+ Indexer provides significant gains in selectivity and execution time related to time-consuming queries and is capable of automatically materializing and dematerializing indexes by predicting next execution times, thus allowing DBAS to perform fewer maintenance and manual configuration tasks related to database index maintenance.

title: Enhanced Weakly Supervised Learning for 3D Hand Pose Estimation
abstract: Accurate 3D hand pose estimation plays a vital role in applications such as augmented reality, virtual reality, robotics and human-computer interaction. Traditional methods rely heavily on fully supervised learning, which demands large-scale 3D annotations that are both expensive and time-consuming to obtain. This study investigates the effectiveness of weakly supervised learning techniques to reduce the reliance on extensive annotations while maintaining high accuracy. We initially implement a ResNet18-based regression model for 3D hand pose estimation and subsequently enhance performance using an optimized EfficientNet-B0 model. The transition to EfficientNet-B0 demonstrates significant improvements in both precision and computational efficiency. Experimental results show that weakly supervised learning not only alleviates the annotation burden but also yields reliable pose estimations suitable for real-time deployment. These findings underscore the feasibility of adopting lightweight, weakly supervised models in practical scenarios, paving the way for more accessible and scalable hand pose estimation systems across various interactive technologies.

title: Multi View Mammogram Analysis with Segmented Breast Masses and Calcifications for BI-RADS Classification
abstract: Breast cancer is considered as the most prevalent cancer among women worldwide. Computer Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems have the ability to obtain promising results in early detection of breast cancer using different imaging techniques. This study focuses on developing a framework to classify segmented mammograms with breast masses and calcifications into the Breast Imaging-Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) categories using multi view mammogram analysis. The proposed method consists of a dual path fine tuned EfficientNetB3 architecture for multi view feature extraction connected to an artificial neural network as the classification head. The suggested approach was evaluated using the INBreast dataset and it achieved an accuracy of 0.88, and a precision of 0.85 which is competitive with the existing methods which only performs the classification to BI-RADS based on a single type of abnormality. According to the results obtained, it can be observed that the proposed multi view approach to classify breast masses and calcifications into BI-RADS categories has an improved accuracy compared to the baseline single view CNN model showing its potential to aid in the early detection of breast cancer accurately. Also, the proposed method can be considered more clinically valid based on the fact that it takes the presence of different types of abnormalities instead of solely considering breast masses or calcifications in mammograms for the classification.

title: From AI Assistance to Critical Thinking: Exploring Cognitive Offloading and Metacognition as Mechanisms Within Personalized Learning Environments
abstract: The rapid adoption of AI-assisted learning tools in higher education has completely transformed the undergraduate study system, but empirical evidence on their impact on deep cognition and learning processes is limited. This study investigates the effects of AI-assisted learning tool usage on metacognition, cognitive offloading, personalized learning, and critical thinking among Sri Lankan undergraduates. Using positivism philosophy and a deductive quantitative approach, data were collected from 379 students in computing, management, and engineering subjects through a 35-items, five-point Likert scale questionnaire, and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings reveal significant direct, indirect, and moderating relationships among key variables, suggesting that the use of AI-assisted learning tools influences students’ learning regulation, reliance on external support, and development of higher-order thinking. This study provides empirical evidence for the cognitive and psychological effects of AI-assisted learning tools, and helps address an important research gap, and offers practical insights for educators, curriculum developers, and policymakers to use balanced and effective AI integration in higher education.

title: Frugal Edge AI: Robust TinyML for Predictive Maintenance in Sri Lankan MSMEs
abstract: The narrative of Industry 4.0 is often defined by high-bandwidth, cloud-centric cyber-physical systems. However, this paradigm is economically and operationally disconnected from the reality of Sri Lanka's manufacturing sector, which is dominated by Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) operating legacy “Brownfield” machinery. This paper proposes a “Frugal Edge AI” framework as a viable alternative to the traditional “Lift and Shift” digital transformation model. By retrofitting legacy equipment—specifically Orthodox Tea Rollers—with ultra-low-power Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) models running on commodity microcontrollers (ESP32), manufacturers can achieve predictive maintenance capabilities without prohibitive Capital Expenditure (CAPEX). We introduce a Spectral Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) feature extraction pipeline capable of isolating mechanical fault signatures even in high-noise industrial environments ($\sigma=0.2$). Simulation results on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) dataset demonstrate that while naive time-domain analysis fails (33.15% accuracy) under industrial noise, our noise-augmented frequency-domain model achieves 98.31% generalized accuracy while consuming only 7.98 KB of flash memory. Crucially, Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) benchmarking on the target ESP32 silicon validates real-time deployment feasibility, confirming an inference latency of 337.56 ms and a peak dynamic RAM usage of just 4.10 KB. Furthermore, comparative benchmarking reveals that optimized Random Forest ensembles offer a superior power-efficiency-to-accuracy ratio compared to lightweight Neural Networks for this specific domain. This confirms that localized, offline processing offers a sustainable path to Industry 5.0 resilience for the Global South. To ensure reproducibility of the “Vaccination Strategy” and quantization results, the source code and CWRU data splits are available at: https://github.com/Conference2026/Frugal-edge-ai.

title: Dynamic Portfolio Allocation in Algorithmic Trading Using Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Market sentiment, as driven by news and online discussion sites is increasingly impacting algorithmic trading systems. In this work, we integrate financial news, social media sentiment gathered from Yahoo news and reddit platform to identify the sentiment related to the market of Bitcoin cryptocurrency. We trained various machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) sentiment classifiers with a dataset of 11,293 Bitcoin-related news headlines extracted from Yahoo Finance and Reddit. In baseline models, Logistic Regression achieved the best performance (accuracy$71.7 \%, F 1=0.704$), and among neural network-based ones, BiLSTM (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) does so with accuracy of 70.5%. The model FinBERT also achieved improved classification performance (accuracy of$83.7 \%, F 1=0.835$), which was further confirmed statically by McNemar's statistical test as compared with the other models. In order to increase the interpretability, Shapley Additive explanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model Agnostic Explanations (LIME) were used to examine the token level contributions to the model decisions, which revealed consistency among the patterns in which the positive and negative terms tend to influence sentiment predictions across the model architecture. This study highlights the importance of incorporating explainability and the sentiment aware modeling into the financial prediction workflows and also provide insights that would be needed for future development of transparent and reliable trading strategies.

title: Explainable AI Models for Predicting Major Complications in Thalassemia Patients
abstract: Thalassemia is an inherited blood disorder in which hemoglobin is synthesized abnormally and requires lifelong blood transfusions and continuous clinical monitoring. Secondary complications such as diabetes and leg ulcers are common, significantly reducing quality of life and increasing healthcare costs. Early detection of these complications is crucial for early intervention. However, the black-box nature of most machine learning algorithms hinders their application in clinical practice. In this study, predictive models for diabetes and leg ulcer complications in thalassemia patients were developed using a clinical dataset with 357 real patient data including demographics, laboratory values, and treatment histories. The models tested were Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Neural Network implemented in PyTorch. The neural network performed best for both complications, with excellent F1-scores and AUC scores. To ensure interpretation, Explainable AI methods were used using SHAP values to identify important clinical risk factors, LIME to produce case-specific explanations, and adversarial reasoning to test operational “what-if” scenarios. The results identified hypogonadism, serum ferritin, hemoglobin, ALT and AST as the best predictors of diabetes and leg ulcers. Through the application of explainable high-performance neural networks, this study demonstrates the potential of Explainable AI systems in improving personalized risk stratification, risk identification, and clinical decision-making for thalassemia management.

title: Sinhala Automatic Text Summarization: Dataset Creation and Comparative Evaluation
abstract: Automatic text summarization for low-resource languages remains a significant challenge in natural language processing, with Sinhala representing a particularly underexplored domain. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to Sinhala text summarization, addressing both dataset scarcity and model development challenges. We introduce a novel Sinhala summarization dataset comprising$\mathbf{2, 4 9 3}$high-quality Sinhala article-summary pairs validated through rigorous human validation (mean scores$>4.0$, Fleiss'$\mathrm{K}>0.60$). We implement and evaluate both extractive and abstractive summarization approaches: extractive methods using TextRank and LexRank with Jensen-Shannon Divergence achieve ROUGE-1 scores up to 0.607, while our fine-tuned Gemma-3-4B model using QLoRA parameterefficient training achieves a ROUGE-1 score of 0.286. While extractive methods currently show higher automatic metric scores, both approaches face challenges that warrant future research. Our dataset and comprehensive baseline evaluation provide a foundation for advancing such future research.

title: Hate Speech Detection with SOCOLD: Sinhala Obfuscated & Code-Mixed Offensive Language Dataset
abstract: Automated detection of hate speech in Sinhala still needs improvements due to the scarcity of resources capable of handling linguistic variations such as obfuscation, Romanized writing, mixed scripts, and Sinhala–English code mixing. Prior studies focus primarily on standard Sinhala or generic code-mixed text and therefore fail to capture the adversarial language patterns widely used on social media platforms. To address this gap, this research introduces SOCOLD, the first-ever dataset specifically designed for the Sinhala Obfuscated and Code-Mixed Offensive Language Dataset, together with three novel linguistic resources: an Obfuscated Sinhala Dictionary, an Emoji-Integrated Offensive Expressions Dictionary, and a Sinhala–English Code-Mixed Offensive Dictionary. These dictionaries enable the effective normalization of distorted, symbol-embedded, and mixed language content and form the core contribution of this work. The novelty of this research lies in the creation of three specialized linguistic dictionaries that collectively provide the first structured approach to normalize intentionally distorted Sinhala hate expressions. Using these dictionaries, machine learning models were trained on 2,000 manually annotated Facebook comments. Classical Machine Learning approaches achieved strong performance, with the Support Vector Classifier reaching 83% accuracy, outperforming transformer-based baselines such as mBERT in this low-resource setting. The dictionaries introduced here provide reusable linguistic infrastructure for future Natural Language Processing research, supporting dataset expansion, advanced model development, and domain adaptation efforts. By improving the reliability of automated hate-speech detection for Sinhala, this work contributes to safer digital communication and more effective moderation in multilingual online communities.

title: Explainability, Risk Modeling, and Segmentation Based Customer Churn Analytics for Personalized Retention in E-Commerce
abstract: In online retail, the cost to attract new customers is higher than retaining existing customers. As a result, businesses invest in predictive analytics for customer churn. However, modern churn prediction algorithms are black boxes that lack the transparency required to identify what actually causes attrition, tenure-based retention, and customer segments with a high risk of churn. Therefore, the next generation of churn analytics focus must shift from prediction to personalized retention. This study proposes a threefold approach that combines explainable AI to describe feature importance insights, survival analysis to model time-to-event data, and finally RFM (recency, frequency, and monetary) approach to segment customers based on transactional behavior. With this explainability, risk modeling, and segmentation-based approach, personalized retention strategies were proposed to reduce attrition and increase customer loyalty. We propose that by following this approach, organizations can determine why churn is likely, when intervention is most effective, and which customer groups to prioritize.

title: Integrating Uncertainty Quantification in AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Industrial Systems
abstract: This research combines Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) with AI for predictive maintenance (PdM), aiming to produce dependable Remaining Useful Life (RUL) predictions and inform risk-managed choices. Recent studies have shown a growing interest in advanced techniques, such as Bayesian deep learning, Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, ensembles, and heteroscedastic regression, across various fields, including aerospace, manufacturing, and energy. Based on these trends, a Bayesian CNN-LSTM model with a dual-head heteroscedastic output is developed using NASA C-MAPSS data to simulate both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. An operational decision rule converts the probabilistic results into maintenance scheduling recommendations. The evaluations demonstrate that the proposed model matches or improves upon the RMSE and MAE of the traditional standard. It also exhibits better calibration, with a lower NLL and a near-nominal PICP, resulting in fewer false alarms and missed detections. These benefits support its use in industrial applications.
