title: Reconstruction of Damaged Sinhala Handwritten Characters with Flow Tangent Guided Strokes
abstract: The reconstruction of damaged Sinhala handwritten characters poses a unique challenge due to the script's complex curvilinear structure, where traditional proximity-based edge linking often fails. To address this limitation, this paper presents a novel approach based on a flow tangent-guided endpoint pairing algorithm and Bezier curvebased stroke restoration. The proposed method extends traditional guided edge linking models by incorporating flowaware tangent vectors, mutual alignment scoring, and global optimization using the Hungarian algorithm. Unlike greedy selection strategies, the proposed approach ensures optimal stroke connectivity even in regions with high combinatorial complexity. Experimental results demonstrate visually accurate restorations and effective character-level repair in structurally complex cases. Evaluation across five damage complexity classes confirms the robustness of the method, achieving over 83.3% accuracy in highly damaged regions and 100% accuracy in simpler cases.

title: Metadata-Aware Agentic Rag Framework for Disaster Response and Task Synthesis
abstract: Timely and contextually accurate information retrieval is a critical challenge in disaster response, where fragmented citizen help requests must be converted into field-executable tasks. While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers a promising solution, standard implementations often lack the operational precision required for high-stakes scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of a standard RAG and a proposed Agentic RAG framework designed for disaster coordination. The Agentic RAG enhances conventional retrieval by integrating adaptive query reformulation, metadata-aware filtering, and iterative self-assessment to improve semantic precision and operational relevance. Both workflows were evaluated over a curated knowledge base of disaster-response documents using an LLM-based judge with a structured rubric to assess outputs on relevance, safety, and specificity. This evaluation methodology itself contributes a reproducible framework for measuring the operational readiness of RAG outputs in this domain. Comparative results demonstrate that the Agentic RAG consistently achieves higher performance, particularly for complex or ambiguous help requests, producing more reliable and actionable guidance. This study provides strong evidence that agentic reasoning is a crucial component for building dependable AI-assisted decision-support systems in critical domains. Compared to the Standard RAG, the Agentic RAG shows a$1.73 \times$fold increase in 'Excellent' judgments, consistent with the fold-change measure commonly used for comparative performance analysis.

title: Knowledge-Guided Graph Neural Networks for Low-Data Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: Molecular property prediction plays a central role in drug discovery, toxicity assessment and computational chemistry. However, most real world datasets in these domains are extremely small and recent large foundation models struggle to generalize in low-data and geometry-sensitive scenarios. To address this problem, we propose a knowledge-guided graph neural network (GNN) framework designed specifically for data-efficient molecular learning. The first contribution is a lightweight architecture that incorporates fundamental chemical priors. These priors such as functional groups and molecular descriptors to guide representation learning without relying on large scale pretraining. The second contribution is transfer learning embedding level knowledge distillation strategy where a pretrained teacher GNN transfers high-level structural knowledge to a compact student model suitable for small molecule datasets. Preliminary expert feedback from 16 domain specialists indicates that the proposed design is both feasible and relevant for drug discovery use cases although experimental validation is planned as future work. The framework is expected to deliver improved performance in cold-start and low data settings. The conceptual study outlines a promising direction for efficient molecular property prediction using knowledge-augmented GNNs.

title: Prioritized Cross-Model Verification System for Hallucination Detection in Black-Box Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities across diverse applications but suffer from hallucinations-generating plausible yet factually incorrect content. This paper presents a prioritized cross-model verification system for detecting hallucinations in black-box LLMs through intelligent multi-LLM consensus mechanisms. A systematic literature review of 15 peerreviewed studies (2020-2025) identified critical gaps: absence of standardized model selection methodologies and limited investigation of heterogeneous ensemble approaches. Addressing these gaps, we developed a practical system employing a heterogeneous ensemble of four diverse LLMs-GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and DeepSeek-V2.5-selected through evidence-based methodology grounded in peer-reviewed benchmark results. The system architecture comprises three tiers: claim extraction using GPT-5, parallel cross-model validation with three dynamically-selected verifiers producing categorical verdicts, and majority voting consensus generating final verdicts. Evaluated on TruthfulQA across 50 questions and 5 target LLMs (250 sessions, 2,260 claims), the system demonstrates strong performance with$\mathbf{8 1. 7 5 \%} \mathbf{F 1}$-score,$\mathbf{7 7. 0 7 \%}$precision, and 87.11% recall-representing 7.6% improvement over previous best zero-resource methods and 31.9% improvement over semantic entropy approaches. At approximately $0.11 per query, the system provides a scalable, production-ready solution for hallucination detection without requiring model internals access.

title: CheX-DFuseNet: Multi-Label Chest Disease Classification Using a Hybrid CNN-ViT Framework with Dynamic Fusion Gate
abstract: Chest diseases remain a major global health burden, and chest X-rays continue to be the most widely used imaging modality for diagnosis. However, multi-label CXR interpretation is challenging due to overlapping disease patterns, strong class imbalance, and the coexistence of focal and diffuse abnormalities. Existing hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer models commonly rely on static or sequential fusion, forcing fixed contributions from local and global features regardless of disease characteristics and often creating information bottlenecks. This paper introduces CheX-DFuseNet, a parallel hybrid CNN-ViT architecture equipped with a Dynamic Fusion Gate that adaptively merges convolutional local features with transformer-based global semantics. Unlike static concatenation or late fusion, the proposed DFG learns token-wise fusion weights through a lightweight MLP, enabling the model to emphasize CNN features for focal diseases and ViT features for diffuse pathologies without requiring explicit disease-type supervision. Experiments were conducted on the NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset using seven baseline and fusion models. The proposed dynamic fusion framework consistently outperformed all static fusion baselines. The best-performing configuration is DFG with weighted BCE and it achieved a Macro AUC of 0.8398, exceeding several state-of-the-art hybrid architectures while remaining computationally efficient. Class-wise AUC analysis further demonstrated improvements in key difficult classes such as Atelectasis, Effusion, and Fibrosis. These findings demonstrate that dynamically adjusting local-global feature contributions is crucial for multi-label CXR classification, and the proposed DFG provides an effective, lightweight alternative to complex attention-based fusion schemes.

title: Quantitative Readability Assessment of Sinhala Handwriting Using Visual Feature Consistency and Sinhala Morphological Feature Matching
abstract: Handwriting legibility is a critical factor in human visual interpretation, distinct from machine recognition accuracy. While readability assessment frameworks exist for Latin scripts, complex Indic scripts like Sinhala remain under-researched. This paper proposes a novel framework for quantitatively evaluating the readability of handwritten Sinhala text using visual and spatial features. The study introduces a feature-driven model incorporating stroke thickness, size consistency, spacing uniformity, slant angle, baseline alignment, and a novel Sinhala morphological feature matching method grounded in the script's unique anatomy. Validation was conducted using a dataset of handwritten samples, each evaluated with subjective ratings provided by native readers on a Likert scale. The proposed framework achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.113, Mean Squared Error (MSE) of$0.019, R^{2}$of 0.233, and a Pearson correlation of 0.509 against human ratings. These results demonstrate the feasibility of automated readability scoring for pedagogical and forensic applications in Sinhala.

title: Cloud-Resilient NDVI Estimation for Smallholder Paddy Fields from Single-Date Sentinel-1 SAR Using an Enhanced U-Net++
abstract: Persistent cloud cover during Sri Lankan monsoons severely limits optical remote sensing for smallholder paddy monitoring. This paper presents a deep learning framework for reconstructing all-weather Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) maps from single-date Sentinel-1 C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery. The method employs an enhanced U-Net++ architecture with a pretrained ResNet34 encoder, spatial and channel squeeze-and-excitation attention, an auxiliary VV/VH backscatter ratio channel, and refined Lee despeckling. Training leverages spatial triplet ensembling for location invariance and a composite loss that combines pixelwise, structural, and perceptual constraints. On a strictly held-out test set from unseen years (2018 and 2025; 2,939,829 pixels), pixel-wise mode aggregation achieves a mean absolute error of 0.1059, root mean square error of 0.1291, and Pearson correlation of 0.556, outperforming published singledate SAR-to-NDVI baselines under temporal out-of-distribution shifts. A simple post-hoc linear calibration restores near-ideal dynamic range with negligible accuracy loss. By eliminating dependence on multi-temporal SAR stacks or cloud-free optical priors, this approach enables near-real-time, high-resolution NDVI estimation in persistently cloudy tropical regions, supporting precision agriculture and food security monitoring.

title: Customer Segmentation and Churn Prediction in the Maritime Shipping Industry Using Machine Learning Techniques: A Sri Lankan Case Study
abstract: Customer churn is a critical issue in industries with high acquisition costs, such as maritime shipping and logistics, where losing a single client can result in substantial financial losses. While churn prediction is well-researched in domains such as telecom and SaaS, limited work has been done in the maritime shipping sector, particularly in Sri Lanka. This research aims to design and deploy a machine learning-based churn prediction and customer segmentation framework tailored for maritime shipping, which uses very common features in the maritime shipping industry. Two primary datasets from the ERP system were combined: the Detailed Income Report, containing financial data, and the operational data report, capturing operational records spanning nine years. Three models were implemented: the logistic regression model, the random forest model, and the XGBoost. As the real-world data had class imbalance present, it was handled using SMOTE for logistic regression and builtin methods for random forest and XGBoost. Results showed that XGBoost achieved the best performance, outperforming the other models. Feature importance analysis revealed the strongest common predictors for the framework. The front-end for the framework was developed using Streamlit and integrated with Power BI for real-time churn monitoring and customer segmentation. This research contributes to filling the gap in maritime churn prediction by demonstrating how machine learning and business intelligence can provide actionable insights for customer retention strategies.

title: ECG Signal Classification for Heart Disease Diagnosis with Deep Learning and Explainable AI: A Sri Lankan Study
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a critical health issue in Sri Lanka, where early and accurate detection is essential for improving patient care. The 12-lead electrocardiogram is a standard diagnostic tool, yet manual interpretation can be time-consuming and error-prone. This study presents a deep learning-based framework for automated classification of electrocardiograms into normal and not_normal categories. A regionspecific dataset was developed from paper-based electrocardiograms collected at Jaffna Teaching Hospital, Sri Lanka, digitized using mobile scanning, and processed into standardized$\mathbf{3} \times \mathbf{4}$lead image formats through segmentation, binarization, and noise reduction. Convolutional neural networks including ResNet-18, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B1, SqueezeNet1.1, and a lightweight DenseNet variant, were trained and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices. ResNet-18 achieved the highest validation accuracy of 93%, followed by SqueezeNet1.1 with$\mathbf{9 0 \%}$. To enhance interpretability, Gradientweighted Class Activation Mapping confirmed that the models emphasized clinically relevant leads and waveforms. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating deep learning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence for reliable Electrocardiogram analysis. The proposed approach offers a scalable decisionsupport pipeline that can aid in the early diagnosis of cardiac abnormalities and contribute to advancing Explainable Artificial Intelligence-driven healthcare solutions in Sri Lanka.

title: Meme-Based Sentiment Shift Prediction in Financial Markets
abstract: The influence of retail investor communities, particularly those on Reddit, has led to a paradigm shift in financial market dynamics, where viral memes often precede significant short-term stock price movements. Traditional sentiment analysis, which relies solely on text, often fails to capture the full expressive context embedded in these artifacts. The aim of this study is to investigate a novel prediction system that integrates the complex visual and textual components of financial memes to forecast stock price shifts. We sought to evaluate the predictive performance of a multimodal sentiment analysis model compared to conventional text-only baselines and to statistically confirm the relationship between meme sentiment and subsequent market behavior. To achieve this, we employed web scraping to collect and analyze 10,000 meme instances. The model utilizes a hybrid deep learning architecture, combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for visual features, Transformers for textual sentiment, and Recurrent Layers to model the temporal flow and virality of the data. The multimodal model achieved 78.54% prediction accuracy, performing comparably to the text-only baseline 79.52%, suggesting that for this specific dataset, textual content remains the primary driver of predictive sentiment. Despite the dominance of text, correlation analysis confirmed a significant relationship between overall meme sentiment and stock price movements$(r=0.6072$and$p<0.0001)$. This work presents a systematic evaluation of meme-based financial prediction, identifying that while multimodal data provides rich context, low-latency predictive systems can prioritize textual analysis for computational efficiency without compromising accuracy.

title: Context-Aware Deep Learning for Waste Classification and Recycling Path Recommendation Towards a Circular Economy
abstract: The shift to a circular economy will require sophisticated waste management systems that can minimize reliance on human sorting and recovery of materials. This study presents a context-aware deep learning framework that not only classifies waste materials but also explicitly links classification outcomes to actionable recycling pathway recommendations, utilizing open-source image datasets. The framework utilizes transfer learning, using MobileNetV2 loaded and trained on ImageNet customized on six waste types (plastic, paper, glass, metal, cardboard, organic). The addition of custom layers, such as a Dense layer with ReLU activation and Dropout rate margin, also aids generalization. The final accuracy score after testing was 78.61%, and a loss of 0.7452 after 10 epochs of training. Beyond classification, the key contribution of the framework is a decisionsupport layer that maps predicted waste categories to contextrelevant recycling pathways, such as composting for organic waste and remanufacturing for glass. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework integrates AI-based classification with process-level improvements in waste management systems, while also promoting recycling behaviors aligned with circular economy objectives, such as reduction, recovery, and recycling. Overall, this framework will aid a more sustainable approach to waste management, while also generating opportunities for future research and combining into a common, coherent, and reproducible method for thousands of smart cities to share information and material recovery facilities (MRFs) to improve their practices and reduce the risk of disposing of waste at landfill facilities.

title: DeFungi Image Classification with Image Enhancement and Feature Fusion
abstract: Timely and accurate identification of fungal infections is crucial for effective clinical diagnosis and agricultural disease management. Traditional microscopic analysis is often limited by high inter-class similarity, subjectivity, and the time-consuming nature of culture-based tests. To address these challenges, this study presents an enhancement-driven feature fusion deep learning framework for efficient microscopic fungi classification. The proposed approach integrates Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalisation (CLAHE) and Median filtering to improve local contrast and suppress noise in fungal micrographs. Enhanced images are processed through pretrained VGG-16, ResNet-18, and ResNet-50 architectures, leveraging different-level feature fusion to combine complementary representations from different enhancement streams. Experiments were conducted using the DeFungi dataset containing 9,114 images across 5 classes. Comparative analysis revealed that ResNet-50 with mid-level different enhanced image feature fusion achieved the highest mean class accuracy of 97.23%, outperforming ResNet-18 (96.47%) and VGG-16 (95.01%), as well as existing state-of-the-art results, while maintaining reasonable training time and computational efficiency. The results demonstrate that enhancement-guided feature fusion significantly improves model robustness, visual discrimination, and generalisation in noisy microscopic environments, offering a simple yet effective solution with lower complexity and resource requirements.

title: AI Automation for Seed Germination with SSD-MobileNetV2 Detection and ESP32 IoT Prototype
abstract: Seed germination assessment is essential for agricultural research but is still predominantly manual, limiting scalability, accuracy, and consistency. To address this, this study presents a low-cost IoT-based germination monitoring system integrating an ESP32 incubator with a lightweight deep-learning detector. The system is designed to support reliable environmental control through sensor-driven regulation of temperature and light, and detect germination using an SSD-MobileNetV2 model under ordinary and light varying imaging conditions. The proposed architecture employs microcontroller-based sensing, actuation, and image acquisition to enable continuous data collection, monitoring, and autonomous operation. Experimental results show that the proposed germination detector achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.83 and average recall (AR) of 0.87, while the light varying identification model achieved mAP of 0.73 and AR of 0.83, indicating moderate robustness under low illumination scenarios. Furthermore, the IoT integration enables remote monitoring, real-time visualization, and automated data logging, improving experimental reproducibility and reducing human effort. Overall, the system offers a scalable, low-cost, and efficient alternative to manual germination testing, with potential for broader application in smart agriculture.

title: Explainable AI for Heart Disease Prediction USING CNNs
abstract: Heart disease remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, causing millions of deaths each year. Accurate and timely diagnosis is essential for effective treatment and prevention, as early detection can reduce complications and improve patient outcomes. Electrocardiography (ECG) provides critical diagnostic information, yet interpreting complex 12-lead signals manually is challenging and prone to human error. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), enable automatic learning of discriminative patterns from ECG data for improved cardiac assessment; however, most CNN and CNN-LSTM models emphasize predictive accuracy while offering limited interpretability. This study presents an InceptionTime-based one-dimensional CNN for multi-label heart disease prediction across five diagnostic superclasses using the PTB-XL dataset. To address the black-box limitation, post-hoc Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods—Grad-CAM and LIME—were applied to highlight model reasoning. Grad-CAM visualizations revealed clinically significant regions, including the QRS complex and ST-segment, while LIME identified lead-specific waveform features most influential for predictions, providing interpretable insights to support clinical decision-making. Unlike intrinsic attention- or case-based approaches, the proposed model integrates complementary post-hoc explanations linking learned representations with physiological meaning. The model achieved a Hamming Score of 88.03% and an AUC of 87.19%, with a subset accuracy of 66.65% providing comprehensive evaluation for multi-label ECG prediction.

abstract_search_text: heart disease remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, causing millions of deaths each year. accurate and timely diagnosis is essential for effective treatment and prevention, as early detection can reduce complications and improve patient outcomes. electrocardiography (ecg) provides critical diagnostic information, yet interpreting complex 12-lead signals manually is challenging and prone to human error. recent advances in deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (cnns), enable automatic learning of discriminative patterns from ecg data for improved cardiac assessment; however, most cnn and cnn-lstm models emphasize predictive accuracy while offering limited interpretability. this study presents an inceptiontime-based one-dimensional cnn for multi-label heart disease prediction across five diagnostic superclasses using the ptb-xl dataset. to address the black-box limitation, post-hoc explainable artificial intelligence (xai) methods—grad-cam and lime—were applied to highlight model reasoning. grad-cam visualizations revealed clinically significant regions, including the qrs complex and st-segment, while lime identified lead-specific waveform features most influential for predictions, providing interpretable insights to support clinical decision-making. unlike intrinsic attention- or case-based approaches, the proposed model integrates complementary post-hoc explanations linking learned representations with physiological meaning. the model achieved a hamming score of 88.03% and an auc of 87.19%, with a subset accuracy of 66.65% providing comprehensive evaluation for multi-label ecg prediction.

title: TSAFN: Temporal Spatial Attention Fusion Network of Alzheimer's Disease Classification in MRI
abstract: The objective of the proposed study is early and accurate classification of Alzheimer's, as well as Temporal-Spatial Attention Fusion Network (TSAFN) operating on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images. Using the publicly available Kaggle Alzheimer's MRI dataset of pictures with four levels of cognitive impairment, such as no impairment, very mild impairment, mild impairment, and moderate impairment, the work applies a group of preprocessing and enhancement strategies to improve the quality of the pictures and diversify the data. The data is divided into training (70), validation (12.5), and testing (17.5) sets. TSAFN is configured to simultaneously segregate both time and space attention features, producing interpretable attention maps that describe AD-influenced brain regions. Training was designed based on the PyTorch template, and the AdamW optimizer, mixed precision computation, and early stopping criteria were used to prevent overfitting. Measurement of performance is done through accuracy, precision, recall, macro-average$\mathbf{F 1}$score, confusion matrices, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC). TSAFN produces a test accuracy of 0.9633 on average, a macro F 1 score of 0.9696, and high ROC-AUC values among the diagnostic classes. The interpretability of the attention maps generates clinically relevant data on AD related neuroanatomical alterations, and therefore, the application of the presented system in research and subsequent clinical applications.

title: Hate Speech Detection in Romanized Sinhala Text Using Multilingual Transformer Models
abstract: Social media has become a key platform for communication, but it has also amplified the spread of hate speech, particularly in languages and dialects that lack digital resources and support. One such case is Romanized Sinhala, an informal writing style commonly used by Sri Lankans. Its irregular spelling, use of phonetic forms, and mixing with English present serious challenges for automatic hate speech detection. This project explores a deep learning-based solution to detect hate speech written in Romanized Sinhala, with the aim of strengthening online safety in low resource language settings. To build the system, the SOLD (Sinhala Offensive Language Dataset) was transliterated into Romanized Sinhala using a custom pipeline. Several state-of-the-art multilingual transformer models, including XLM-RoBERTa, IndicBERT, and distil-mBERT, were evaluated to identify the most effective approach. Among them, multilingual BERT (mBERT) achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 81.28%, F1-score of 0.78, and recall of 0.81 after fine-tuning on the Romanized dataset. These findings highlight that pre-trained multilingual models, when adapted appropriately, can be effective even for languages with limited digital infrastructure. Beyond technical outcomes, this project has broader social relevance. It provides a foundation for developing tools that can reduce harmful content in Sinhala-speaking online communities, support moderation efforts, and promote healthier digital spaces in Sri Lanka.

title: A physics-informed machine learning for detecting suspicious satellite maneuvers (orbital manipulation)
abstract: Satellite systems have become prime targets for cyberthreats given their critical role in global infrastructure and general lack of security. Among these, orbital manipulation, a form of satellite hijacking, is a particularly severe threat that can disrupt essential operations and impact national security. To address these concerns, this research proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based anomaly detection system that utilizes Machine Learning (ML) models to analyze telemetry data for possible orbital manipulations with a multi-gate physics architecture grounded in orbital mechanics, to verify that detected anomalies are kinematically inconsistent and are therefore genuine integrity failures. This research demonstrates that temporal-based models like LSTM are essential for this domain, achieving high recall rates which are then validated by the physics component. While the framework includes multiple physical constraints, this study specifically validates the energy-based Vis-Viva gate, with the Tsiolkovsky and Angular Momentum gates established as architectural designs for future verification. This study concludes that successful AI deployment in orbital cybersecurity requires a comprehensive approach that integrates domain-specific context and physics-informed validation beyond traditional performance metrics

title: Robust Bus Dwell Time Predictive Machine Learning Model by Handling Real Concept Drift
abstract: Precise and reliable forecasting of dwell time at each bus stop helps passengers and operators in the urban and rural areas of developing countries that have heterogeneous traffic conditions. Existing studies have proposed various approaches to predict bus dwell time accurately. However, beyond the predictable patterns of seasonal changes, there can be unpredictable changes. In heterogeneous traffic conditions, the effect of these changes is multitudinal and further exacerbated. It may cause a deterioration in the accuracy of the existing bus dwell time predictive models. This phenomenon is known as concept drift. Therefore, we propose a robust strategy to handle concept drift that employs the active strategy with Drift Detection Method (DDM) and incremental learning. Further, we introduce the hybrid batch processing technique to eliminate the issues that arise when formulating data batches. The proposed approach achieved a 17.35% improvement in terms of mean absolute error (MAE) when compared to the XGBoost-based bus dwell time predictive model and achieved 2.04% lower MAE and 55.28% reduction in MAPT compared to the baseline concept drift handling strategy. Despite the presence of concept drift, our strategy can result in a robust model capable of predicting bus dwell time accurately while adapting to dynamic changes.

title: Developing a Sinhala Speech Recognition System Using Whisper
abstract: The demand for accurate and robust speech recognition in low-resource languages has increased significantly in recent years. Sinhala, despite being spoken by over 17 million people, remains underrepresented in Automatic Speech Recognition research due to the limited availability of annotated datasets and its linguistic complexity. This study presents the development of a Sinhala Automatic Speech Recognition system by fine-tuning OpenAI's Whisper model on a curated and augmented Sinhala speech dataset. A combined dataset of 3078 clips (5.83 hours) was expanded to 12312 clips (23.32 hours) using multiple augmentation techniques. Fine-tuning was performed on individual datasets and their combinations, both with and without augmentation, to evaluate the impact of dataset diversity. Experimental results show that the zero-shot Whisper models performed very poorly on Sinhala. However, fine-tuning significantly improved performance. The Whisper medium model, trained on an augmented news-style custom dataset, achieved a Word Error Rate of 5%. These results confirm the importance of dataset quality, augmentation, and multi-source training for improving ASR in low-resource languages. Furthermore, a lightweight web interface was developed to enable real-time Sinhala speech-to-text transcription. This work demonstrates that fine-tuned multilingual ASR models can bridge the resource gap for Sinhala Language.

title: A Machine Learning Based Approach for Detection and Classification of Fault and Fault Location in Medium Voltage Power System
abstract: Reliable and safe electrical power systems are essential to sustain modern living and industrial operations. Quick and accurate detection and localization of faults are essential for minimizing their impact and restoring normal operation. This paper presents a machine-learning-based pipeline for fault detection, multi-class classification, and fault-location estimation on a 33 kV distribution feeder in Nintavur, Sri Lanka. Real measurements from the CEB Nintavur Customer Service Centre (CSC) were digitized and modeled in ETAP to create realistic simulation data. Two stages of training were performed: initially using sample datasets generated under two feature regimes—faulty-phase-only and all-phases—and subsequently using a real-data-derived dataset. On the sample datasets, the CNN and SVM achieved 100% accuracy in the all-phase regime but less than 50% in the faulty-phase-only regime, confirming the advantage of full-phase information. On the real-data-derived dataset (240 buses, 560 samples), CNN reached 99.40% classification accuracy with a fault-location RMSE of 0.46 km, while SVM achieved 98.81% accuracy with 1.01 km RMSE. Both models provided real-time inference capability with fault-clearance decisions within 1 s. Although CNN required a longer training time compared to SVM, it consistently delivered superior performance and robustness, validating its suitability for deployment in medium-voltage feeders.

title: A Framework for Sequence Classification in Medical Diagnostics Using Machine Learning
abstract: Contemporary healthcare generates massive volumes of sequential data, including time stamped clinical events, biomedical signals, and genomic sequences. This paper presents a multimodal machine learning framework for simultaneous detection of chronic kidney disease (CKD), liver disease, and cardiac abnormalities by integrating structured blood based laboratory markers with raw 12-lead ECG signals. The system comprises a LightGBM based classifier for tabular biomarkers, a ConvNeXt1D convolutional model for temporal ECG feature extraction, and a unified multimodal fusion architecture for joint multi task prediction. Models were trained and evaluated on public clinical datasets with stratified sampling, threshold optimization, and calibration to ensure robustness and fairness. Results show strong CKD performance from the lab-test model (AUROC$\approx 0.97, \text{F1} \approx 0.95$), moderate performance for liver disease (AUROC$\approx 0.72$), and effective arrhythmia classification by the ECG model, with challenges persisting for rare classes. The fusion model outperformed both unimodal components across all disease categories, particularly in imbalanced or ambiguous cases by leveraging complementary physiological and biochemical signals. Interpretability methods, including SHAP for lab-test features and attention weighted pooling for salient ECG segments, provided clinically aligned explanations, while the fusion mechanism enabled cross modal attribution. Overall, the framework offers a scalable, interpretable, and clinically grounded approach that generalizes across heterogeneous medical data and multimorbid conditions, supports extension to additional modalities or diseases, and lays the foundation for future clinical deployment and real-world validation.

title: Developing a Data-Driven Credit Scoring System and Optimal Fund Allocation Framework for E-Commerce Merchants
abstract: The rapid expansion of global e-commerce has outpaced the ability of traditional financial institutions to assess merchant creditworthiness, particularly for micro-sellers lacking formal financial histories. To address this “cold start” problem, this study develops a dual-modeling credit scoring and fund allocation framework using alternative operational data from the Brazilian Olist dataset (2016-2018). Sellers with at least six months of activity and over 80 orders were selected to match institutional eligibility criteria. The methodology integrates a supervised learning approach, comparing Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGB) trained on business-defined proxy labels, with an unsupervised Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to validate latent risk structures. The HGB model emerged as the superior predictor, achieving a One-vs-Rest AUC of 0.95 and robust probability calibration. The unsupervised GMM (K=3, selected via BIC) independently corroborated the performance hierarchy, confirming the stability of the engineered features. Furthermore, the study translates these scores into a dynamic fund allocation framework, mapping risk bands (A-E) to specific financing caps (30%-100% of receivable value). This research provides a scalable, data-driven solution for financial inclusion, enabling lenders to automate risk-sensitive funding decisions in data-scarce digital marketplaces.

abstract_search_text: the rapid expansion of global e-commerce has outpaced the ability of traditional financial institutions to assess merchant creditworthiness, particularly for micro-sellers lacking formal financial histories. to address this “cold start” problem, this study develops a dual-modeling credit scoring and fund allocation framework using alternative operational data from the brazilian olist dataset (2016-2018). sellers with at least six months of activity and over 80 orders were selected to match institutional eligibility criteria. the methodology integrates a supervised learning approach, comparing logistic regression, random forest, and histogram-based gradient boosting (hgb) trained on business-defined proxy labels, with an unsupervised gaussian mixture model (gmm) to validate latent risk structures. the hgb model emerged as the superior predictor, achieving a one-vs-rest auc of 0.95 and robust probability calibration. the unsupervised gmm (k=3, selected via bic) independently corroborated the performance hierarchy, confirming the stability of the engineered features. furthermore, the study translates these scores into a dynamic fund allocation framework, mapping risk bands (a-e) to specific financing caps (30%-100% of receivable value). this research provides a scalable, data-driven solution for financial inclusion, enabling lenders to automate risk-sensitive funding decisions in data-scarce digital marketplaces.

title: Real-Time Emotion and Facial Expression-Driven Human-Computer Interaction for Personalized Experiences
abstract: This paper presents a real-time multimodal humancomputer interaction (HCI) system that integrates facial expression recognition, speech-based command execution, and hand gesture-driven mouse control to enable a natural and accessible interaction experience. Interpretation of facial expression is done through MediaPipe FaceMesh, which identifies 468 dense face landmarks converted into geometric and motion-derived features. These characteristics are classified using a Random Forest model to define universal emotions. The identified emotions provide context-specific feedback without interfering with OS functionality. Speech recognition with a configurable wake word allows hands-free control, utilizing a hybrid intent recognizer that combines template-based rules with a cloud-supported language model. Intents have resolutions to lower level system functions such as application loading and media handling. MediaPipe Hands is also used to record the landmarks on hands so as to map gestures like index pointing and pinches to mouse clicks, allowing touchless control of the cursor, clicking and scrolling. The multimodal design is incorporated with the low latency to guarantee simultaneous operation of all modules smoothly. Experimental results demonstrate that these combined modalities create a responsive and accessible platform, increasing usability and personalization.

title: Enhancing Human-AI Collaboration in Management Decision Making: An Empirical Framework for Decision Support in Digital Transformation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now woven into everyday organizational processes, making human-AI collaboration a decisive factor in digital transformation. Yet most studies have examined trust or explainability in isolation, leaving little guidance on how psychological and cognitive factors jointly shape outcomes. This study develops and validates a model where trust, transparency, and cognitive load predict managerial decision quality. A pilot survey$(\mathbf{n} \boldsymbol{=} \mathbf{1 0 0})$confirmed instrument reliability, followed by a large-scale survey of 758 managers, academics, and professionals in Sri Lanka. Analyses in SPSS showed strong reliability$(\alpha=0.969$0.983). Trust$(\mathrm{r}=0.629, \mathrm{p}<.001)$and transparency$(\mathrm{r}=0.389$,$\mathrm{p}<.001)$improved decision outcomes, while cognitive load$(\mathrm{r}$= -0.547,$p<.001)$reduced them. Regression confirmed these effects, with the three predictors explaining 85.8% of variance$\left(\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.858\right)$. The findings validate a robust framework and offer practical guidance for designing AI interfaces, strengthening governance, and training managers to collaborate effectively with AI. By addressing human factors, organizations can optimize decision-making during digital transformation.

title: Enhancing Digital Image Forensics: a Comparative Analysis on Deep Learning Frameworks for Copy-Move Forgery Detection
abstract: The rapid development of digital image manipulation technologies has made image forgery detection a critical area of research in cyber forensics. Copy-move forgery is one of the most common forms of image manipulation. This involves copying and pasting a region within the same image to hide or duplicate the original content. Traditional detection methods are often ineffective in detecting geometric transformations done on images such as scaling, rotation, and compression. Deep learning technologies have significantly advanced image forensics. However, there is limited research that compares different neural network architectures used for copy-move forgery detection. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of five deep learning models (CNN, GAN, RNN, ResNet50, and VGG16) evaluated on three benchmark datasets to identify their effectiveness in detecting copy-move forgeries. Each deep learning model consists of unique features and capabilities, thus enabling a detailed investigation of their strengths, limitations, and suitability for various manipulation scenarios. Preprocessing steps included normalization, rotation, scaling, and contrast enhancement to ensure robustness. We evaluated the impact of different model parameters on each selected deep learning model. Experimental results show that CNN achieved the highest training accuracy (93.8%). The VGG16 and ResNet50 outperformed (88% and 80% respectively), but not higher than the CNN. The outcomes provide valuable insights about the influence of architectural design on copy-move forgery detection performance. Also contribute toward guiding future forensic model development.

title: Enhanced Environmental Sound Classification with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
abstract: Environmental Sound Classification (ESC) demonstrates many potential applications in several domains such as smart homes, smart cities, environment surveillance systems and many more. Despite its importance, such systems prevail over several challenges that have not been addressed. More practical challenges such as being able to deploy in edge devices as well as challenges related to robustness and explainability are equally important when considering real world implementation. Current classification methods mostly include Artificial Neural Networks and traditional machine learning approaches. Recent research in machine learning, presents strategies inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold Knowledge representation to develop more efficient neural networks which are quite different to traditional neural networks. This special neural network type is known as Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks. This work presents study of application of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for ESC. The novel hybrid neural network architecture could achieve an accuracy of (98.05±0.29)% with model size 30.87 MB.

title: Restoring Sinhala Text at Word and Letter Level Using a Masked Language Model and Statistical Fusion
abstract: Text restoration in low-resource and morphologically rich languages like Sinhala presents unique challenges due to data scarcity and complex linguistic structures. This research proposes a hybrid approach that leverages fine-tuned Masked Language Models (MLMs), specifically RoBERTa, combined with classical statistical language models—n-gram and Bag-of-Words (BoW)—to restore missing or corrupted words and letters in Sinhala text.in restoring incomplete Sinhala text at both word and character levels. The system performs restoration at sentence, word, and letter levels by combining deep contextual modeling with surface-level frequency statistics. The model was trained on a Physics-domain Sinhala corpus derived from G.C.E Advanced Level materials and evaluated on a validation set of Sinhala sentences. The proposed MLM + N-gram fusion achieves the highest sentence-level accuracy and lowest Word Error Rate (WER), and Character Error Rate (CER), outperforming both the MLM-only and MLM + BoW baselines. These results highlight the effectiveness of shallow fusion in low-resource contexts and demonstrate the benefit of integrating contextual prediction with statistical fluency constraints. The approach offers a practical and extensible framework for automated text restoration, with potential applicability to other underresourced languages and noisy text domains.

title: TryOnAI: Revolutionizing Online Shopping with Augmented Reality and Deep Learning for Virtual Try-Ons and Size Prediction
abstract: In the fashion industry, Augmented Reality (AR) is changing how customers experience garments; this holds good, especially in custom clothing. This research aims at resolving the problem of how a customer and a vendor can view the visualization of garment fitting correctly online. The research design an interactive fitting room system using AR that allows customers to interactively visualize garments and find their size accurately for a vendor. This will be done with the support of Marvelous Designer for the design of realistic 3D garment models and Lens Studio for the development of AR sessions in virtual try-ons. The main components of the system were precise garment modeling, integration of AR technologies, and development of a size prediction feature based on anthropometric measurements. As methods used in this research, there were data collection, 3D garment creation, AR session development, and integration of the back-end and front-end of the system. The results show a general user-friendly experience with a high accuracy of size recommendations and realism in garment visualization, which led to increased satisfaction among both customers and vendors. This approach has already indicated vast potential for the improvement of online shopping experiences in the fashion industry.

title: Hybrid approach for information retrieval in Sri Lankan legal domain
abstract: Information retrieval in the legal domain has become a significant research area due to the specific nature of the language in the legal domain [1]. This complexity is further exacerbated in contexts such as Sri Lanka, where English literacy rates among individuals aged 15 and above are approximately 22%, posing a significant barrier to comprehending intricate legal documentation [2]. Current solutions present a trade-off: traditional keyword searches require technical vocabulary that lay users lack, whereas generic LLMs offer conversational ease but frequently 'hallucinate' or misrepresent local statutes [3]. To address this, we propose a hybrid system combining precise document retrieval with a domain-adapted LLM [4]. Our approach finetunes Gemma-3-4B-IT [5] on Sri Lankan legal data [6], combining exact statutory retrieval with simplified summaries for lay audiences.

title: HARNESSING AI FOR ACADEMIC RESILIENCE: A MIXED METHOD STUDY ON POSTGRADUATE STRESS AND WELL-BEING IN SRI LANKAN UNIVERSITIES
abstract: This study investigates the escalating mental health challenges faced by postgraduate students in Sri Lankan universities, focusing on stress and well-being. The study involved 110 full-time postgraduate students aged 22–35 from the Open University of Sri Lanka and the University of Colombo. Using a mixed-methods approach, quantitative data were gathered through the DASS-21 questionnaire, analyzed with machine learning algorithms and sentiment analysis to identify stress patterns, while qualitative insights were obtained from threeweek interactions with the Wysa chatbot. Results revealed that 68% of participants exhibited moderate to severe stress, with academic pressure (37.5%) and financial concerns (25%) as key contributors. The chatbot intervention reduced anxiety in 65% of participants, with significant improvement in DASS-21 scores (p < 0.001). This study demonstrates AI’s potential as a scalable, culturally adaptable tool for improving mental health support in universities. It highlights the need for long-term studies, integration into institutional frameworks, and consideration of cultural and financial barriers for sustainable adoption.

title: AI-powered mobile assistant for precision cinnamon farming using real-time weather and soil data in the southern part of Sri Lanka
abstract: Ceylon cinnamon (Cinnamomum verum) is a globally renowned agricultural product and a key contributor to Sri Lanka’s economy, particularly in the Southern Province. However, cinnamon farmers face persistent challenges due to climate variability, declining soil health, and limited access to real-time, localized agricultural insights, leading to suboptimal decision-making. To address these issues, this study presents the design, development, and evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered mobile assistant aimed at enhancing precision cinnamon farming through the integration of real-time weather forecasts and soil condition data. The system was developed using the Flutter framework with Firebase backend services, incorporating RESTful Application Programming Interface (API)s for weather and soil data integration, while TensorFlow Lite enables on-device AI inference to ensure low-latency recommendations. Random Forest is used for predictive analytics, providing personalized, location-specific recommendations on irrigation scheduling, fertilization, plantation planning, and pest management. The assistant also supports multilingual interactions in Sinhala and Tamil, improving accessibility for rural farmers. Data were sourced from the Sri Lankan Department of Agriculture, meteorological services, public weather APIs, and scientific literature, complemented by field surveys and controlled experiments across three cinnamon cultivation sites over 6 months. The evaluation involved 20 AI-assisted farmers and a control group of 20 farmers following traditional practices. Field trials showed significant improvements: crop yields increased by 8-12%, water usage decreased by 15%, fertilizer usage reduced by 10%, and pesticide use lowered by 7% without compromising productivity. Over 80% of participants reported high satisfaction, citing usability and multilingual support as key enablers. This solution addresses gaps in existing agricultural platforms by delivering real-time, localized decision support tailored to the cinnamon sector. Future enhancements will integrate pest detection, disease prediction, and broader regional deployment, contributing to climate-resilient, sustainable, and data-driven agriculture in Sri Lanka.

title: Predictive Models for Urban Air Quality Management Using AI
abstract: Air pollution threatens public health in datascarce urban areas like Sri Lanka, where sparse monitoring hinders proactive management. We propose an integrated AI framework: hybrid SARIMAX-Temporal Fusion Transformer for multi-pollutant forecasting, ensemble spatial estimation for gap-filling, CEEMDAN-Seq2Seq for 24-hour AQI risk alerting, GRU for anomaly detection, and XAI for transparency. Validated on Central Environmental Authority data (20192024), the model achieves an 81.6% decrease in the value of the RMSE metric for ozone forecasting, as well as an R2 value of 0.9077 for high-risk AQI prediction, outperforming the baseline methods by 15-81%. The framework is modular in nature, thereby providing policymakers with the ability to use real-time dashboards, thus making Sri Lanka move from reactive to proactive management.

title: Real-Time Vision-Based Human—Robot Interaction Framework for Low-Cost Embedded Robotic Arms
abstract: Low-cost robotic manipulation remains inaccessible to many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) due to hardware cost and programming complexity. Conventional robotic control approaches rely heavily on inverse kinematic modelling and geometric calibration, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained settings. This paper presents a real-time vision-based human-robot interaction framework for controlling a 4-DOF robotic arm using a monocular RGB camera and embedded wireless actuation. Human joint angles are geometrically extracted using MediaPipe pose estimation, filtered via a discrete Kalman estimator, and directly mapped to servo actuation without inverse kinematics. The perception-processing-actuation pipeline operates at approximately 10 FPS under bounded Wi-Fi delay. Experimental results demonstrate a mean latency of 57.3 ms and inter-frame angular variation below 4 degrees across all joints. The results confirm stable real-time imitation control using a lightweight, embedded-compatible architecture suitable for educational and SME deployment.

title: Reimagining academic integrity framework in the age of AI: An ethical approach
abstract: The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) such as generative tools like ChatGPT, has resulted in their unprecedented use in everyday life. While these tools have proven to be useful, efficient and user friendly appealing to many fields, they have also arguably created a disruptive impact on academia to a certain extent, challenging universities to rethink their traditional understanding of academic integrity. In particular, the transformation involving AI has compelled state universities in Sri Lanka to reimagine the notions of authorship, originality and academic misconduct and take initiatives to reform their existing academic integrity frameworks. title: An Interpretable Multimodal AI Framework for Severity-Aware and Guideline-Aligned Treatment Recommendation in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria
abstract: Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (CSU) is a recurrent inflammatory disorder characterized by fluctuating disease severity and variable therapeutic response, requiring continuous monitoring and guideline-aligned treatment. Current artificial intelligence approaches for urticaria primarily focus on image-based lesion analysis and do not integrate heterogeneous clinical evidence for therapeutic decision support. In this study, we propose an interpretable multimodal clinical decision support framework that jointly analyzes dermatological images, laboratory biomarkers, and clinical text narratives to model disease severity and support drug-class recommendation. The framework employs a task-conditioned gated fusion mechanism to adaptively combine modality-specific information in alignment with established treatment guidelines. The proposed approach was evaluated on 3000 patient-level CSU records using patient-level data partitioning. An image-only EfficientNet-B3 baseline achieved 68% accuracy in drug-class prediction, whereas the multimodal gated fusion model achieved 82.3% accuracy with a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.81. These results demonstrate that integrating multimodal clinical evidence substantially improves therapeutic modeling reliability and supports clinically aligned decision-making in CSU management.

title: Akura: Adaptive Sinhala Learning for Early Childhood Using Gesture, Voice, Emotion and Handwriting
abstract: Early childhood Sinhala language education in Sri Lanka faces persistent challenges such as large class sizes, reliance on rote-based learning, lack of personalized engagement, and limited engaging content, resulting in poor early literacy outcomes. This research presents Akura, a novel multimodal mobile platform that integrates real-time handwriting recognition, gesture-based numeracy, emotion-aware lesson adaptation, and speech pronunciation feedback to deliver an interactive and personalized Sinhala learning experience for children aged 3-6. The system is optimized to run entirely on low-end mobile devices and uses on-device intelligence to ensure data privacy and low latency. Each module of Akura's multimodal approach has been designed with child-specific optimizations to dynamically adjust feedback, lesson difficulty, and content in real time according to each child's performance and emotional state, while generating progress reports that summarize learning outcomes and interaction trends for caregivers and educators. The study yielded an 8.1% error rate for the speech pronunciation assessment model and 92.5% accuracy for the emotion classification model. Additionally, the gesture recognition model achieved 93.4% accuracy, and the real-time handwriting recognition module achieved 95% accuracy through active stroke-level validation. To validate real-world applicability, Akura underwent technical validation on low-end mobile devices and an educational impact assessment with 30 preschoolers. By fusing multimodal sensing, Akura targets improved engagement and measurable gains in early Sinhala literacy and numeracy. Overall, addressing the critical gap left by existing static Sinhala applications, this work introduces a novel end-to-end multimodal framework for Sinhala early-childhood education that is deployable offline and suitable for resource-constrained settings.

title: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Pest Classification: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: ABSTRACT The protection of crops from pests is essential for sustainable agriculture and global food security. Traditional pest identification techniques that are based on visual examination are time‐consuming and prone to errors. Recent developments in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) and specifically deep learning (DL) enabled pests to be detected accurately and automatically. This review systematically examines DL‐based approaches, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transformer models, ensemble methods, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), for pest classification, with an emphasis on benchmark datasets, model architectures, and evaluation metrics. Transformer models, such as GNViT, achieved 99.52% accuracy and a 90.9% F1‐score on the IP102 dataset, which is approximately 10% higher than the CNNs. The Vision Transformer (ViT) model achieved 96.7% accuracy on PlantVillage. The ensemble model, like GAEnsemble, achieved excellent accuracies of 98.81% and 95.16% on D0 and SCD, respectively. CNN models had relatively lower performance on the IP102, and the GNNs showed poor performance (below 60%). This paper discusses prospective methodological enhancements, current limitations, and future prospects for developing scalable, understandable, and multi‐domain pest classification systems.

title: Too familiar to ignore, but too different to tolerate: The role of the law in regulating emotional expression by robots to mitigate the harmful effects of robot deception
abstract: A long-standing argument for why robots will never “take over” and pose an existential threat to humans is that we will always have a “kill switch” to deactivate them. But what if a robot manipulates us into not flipping that switch? Recent studies show that robots are capable of deception. Despite ongoing debates regarding the specific nature of this capability, such as whether it is indicative of a theory of mind or consciousness, robot deception (RD) can be “intentional” from at least a behaviorist point of view. The expression/mimicking of emotions is one of the most effective ways in which robots engage in deception. This poses unique ethical and regulatory challenges because it is not ostensibly malicious or threatening. The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AIA) currently establishes the most comprehensive framework for the regulation of robots and provides a starting point to assess the efficacy of contemporary regulatory standards. Thus, this paper will involve a conceptual/normative analysis of RD combined with a doctrinal analysis of the AIA. title: Predictive analytics for rice canopy microclimate using weather forecast data and BG-358 monitoring
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa) is a primary food source for over half the global population, yet its yield is increasingly threatened by climate-induced microclimatic variations, particularly during sensitive growth stages like flowering. This study presents the development of a Machine Learning (ML)-based Early Warning System (EWS) designed to predict adverse canopy microclimate conditions, specifically temperature, humidity, and wind that influence rice yield and spikelet sterility. Utilizing high-resolution microclimatic data from the BG-358 rice canopy monitoring system, a locally developed IoT-based platform for real-time monitoring of microclimate, data were collected at 2-minute intervals from 2019 to 2024, resulting in a dataset of approximately 200,000 data points for two flowering seasons (each nearly 1 month) per year at RRDI Bathalagoda. These data, combined with NASA global forecast inputs, were split into 70% for training and 30% for testing, ensuring robust evaluation and reliable predictions to support proactive agricultural decision-making. The study employed Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Neural Networks to predict canopy temperature, relative humidity (RH), and wind conditions. After data pre-processing, including normalization and temporal feature engineering, models were evaluated using MAE, RMSE, and R² metrics. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior performance with an MAE of 0.78 °C, RMSE of 1.15 °C, and R² of 0.91 for temperature prediction. RH and wind predictions also showed high accuracy, with RH remaining above the 60% critical threshold in most cases, though wind forecasts, especially above the 20 km/h threshold, exhibited greater variability due to localized microclimatic conditions. Integrating real-time canopy data with weather forecasts enhanced prediction robustness, enabling heat-induced spikelet sterility anticipation up to 48 hours in advance with 85% reliability. The developed EWS incorporates real-time dashboards and automated alerts, demonstrating strong potential in mitigating climate-related rice yield losses and supporting sustainable agriculture. Future work will expand datasets across varieties and regions and foster collaboration with agricultural stakeholders for wider adoption and broader-scale yield forecasting to strengthen food security planning.

title: Multisensory Learning Tools for Improving Skills in Down Syndrome Children Using Deep Learning
abstract: Children with Down syndrome face several significant challenges in developing countries like Sri Lanka. The purpose of this research is to explore a new approach to enhancing the educational, social, and personal development of children with Down syndrome, aged 5 to 10, in Sri Lanka through the use of deep learning technologies such as CNN and LSTM. This project aims to deliver an affordable platform that offers children with Down syndrome a low-cost, effective, discreet, reliable, and modern educational service. The platform provides educational support in four main areas—handwriting, verbal communication, mathematics, and gross motor skills—specifically tailored for children with Down syndrome. It utilizes deep learning technology to offer real-time, accurate feedback, enabling children to engage in exercises at home. This technical education system improves the quality of life for these children, particularly in a country like Sri Lanka, where many people are not familiar with information technology, by being both affordable and easy to use.

title: Advanced Technologies for Skill Enhancement and Talent Recognition
abstract: Children with Down Syndrome encounter significant challenges in speech articulation, cognitive development and learning, which conventional educational approaches often struggle to address effectively. Difficulties in speech clarity, working memory and problem-solving highlight the need for adaptive learning solutions tailored to their unique needs. To address these challenges, EnlightenDS developed an artificial Intelligence system combined with educational technology that enhances learning through detection, pronunciation training, mathematics exercises and talent identification. The early detection of developmental concerns, facilitating timely intervention and module leverages support vector machine to assess the detection of Down Syndrome. The pronunciation training component integrates natural language processing and a flask-based API to process speech input, utilising google speech-to-text API and DeepSpeech AI for pronunciation evaluation. Speech-to-text conversion and phoneme-level articulation analysis further refine speech feedback. The mathematics training module applies structured learning methodologies like Kumon, Stern, and Numicon, ensuring an adaptive learning experience. Additionally, the talent identification system employs AI-driven implementation and machine learning based analysis to monitor engagement in learning, drawing, and motor activities, recognizing each child's talents and interests. Evaluation of EnlightenDS demonstrates that AI-powered assessment and personalised learning techniques significantly improve cognitive abilities and speech development while creating a more engaging educational experience. These findings emphasize the potential of AI, image processing and adaptive learning methodologies in special education, fostering enhanced communication, cognitive growth and talent recognition for children with Down Syndrome.

title: AI-Driven Prediction of Optimal Player Positions Based on Fundamental Skills in Netball
abstract: This research presents an innovative, video-based performance monitoring system designed to assess and enhance the fundamental skills of netball players while predicting optimal playing positions. Using advanced computer vision and machine learning techniques, the system evaluates fundamental skills through automated video analysis. The framework integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), with feature extraction powered by pre-trained ResNet50 models, and temporal sequence analysis using Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. In addition, random forest classifiers, supported by SMOTE-balanced data sets, are used for accurate position prediction. The system also incorporates centroid-based motion tracking through OpenCV, enabling precise monitoring of player movements. Unlike traditional subjective coaching methods, data-driven insights offer tailored training recommendations. The predictive analytics component also anticipates player development trajectories and role assignment. By transforming conventional netball training into an AI-driven predictive process, this research provides a powerful tool for coaches and players, improving skill evaluation accuracy, optimizing player positioning, and fostering informed evidence-based decision-making. Ultimately, this innovation contributes to improved individual performance, more cohesive team dynamics, and increased competitive success.

title: Automated Advanced Acne Lesion Analysis And Monitoring With Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Acne is a prevalent chronic inflammatory skin condition that significantly impacts the quality of life and mental health of individuals worldwide. Current diagnostic methods often rely on manual assessments by dermatologists, which can be subjective, time-consuming, and inconsistent across practitioners. Although several automated acne detection models have been proposed in recent literature, limitations such as inadequate performance across diverse skin tones, insufficient severity classification, and lack of longitudinal monitoring remain challenges. This research addresses these gaps by proposing an advanced AI-driven system that integrates deep learning models for both acne lesion detection and severity grading, alongside a monitoring mechanism to track healing progression over time. A custom dataset, validated by dermatologists and enriched with images from Kaggle and DermNet, was used for model training and evaluation. Comparative analysis with existing architectures, such as VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, and Siamese networks, demonstrated that the customized CNN model achieved a 93.25% accuracy in acne detection, while a tailored CNN model achieved 72.07% accuracy in acne severity classification, aiding dermatologists in tailoring treatments and improving patient outcomes.

abstract: Conventional CCTV (Closed-Circuit Television) surveillance systems capture continuous video streams without intelligence, resulting in storage overhead, delayed incident response, and inability to differentiate human activity from irrelevant motion. This paper presents CCTV IntelliGuard, a lightweight edge-based module that enhances traditional CCTV systems with real-time human motion detection and logging. The system employs a hybrid approach combining OpenCV based motion detection with YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) object detection model [1], deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device. Upon detecting human activity and the system records timestamped video clips. This retrofit solution transforms conventional CCTV into intelligent surveillance with minimal additional infrastructure. title: A Mobile Application to Enhance Skills in Children with Nonverbal Learning Disability
abstract: Nonverbal Learning Disability (NVLD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder affecting children, characterized by strong verbal skills but significant challenges in visual-spatial processing, motor skills, and communication. This paper introduces a mobile application designed to address these challenges through interactive and personalized activities. The app leverages machine learning and artificial intelligence to improve visual-spatial abilities, communication skills, and cognitive development. By engaging children in pattern recognition, word recognition, and touch screen integration, the app aims to enhance critical thinking, decision-making, and relationship identification in children aged 10-13. The algorithms used in this research are the Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment Algorithm, Random Forest Classifier, Real-Time Object Detection Algorithm, and Deep Q-Network (DQN). This paper explores the development, features, and impact of the app in supporting children with NVLD.

title: AI Agent Based Customer Risk Prediction and Document Automation in Motor Insurance
abstract: This study presents an integrated agentic workflow c ombining m achine l earning (ML) a nd l arge language models (LLMs) to automate motor insurance risk assessment and document processing. The system employs an XGBoost model trained on historical claims data to predict customer risk, augmented by Llama 3.3 70B for generating business insights. A LangGraph-based workflow a gent o rchestrates risk evaluation, LLM-driven explanations, and vehicle-type-specific actions. Additionally, document automation leverages OpenCV for classification a nd G emini 1.5 F lash f or i nformation extraction. Experimental results demonstrate 92.3% risk prediction accuracy, 88% document classification p recision, a nd significant reductions in manual processing time. The synergy of ML and LLMs enables scalable, explainable decision-making in the insurance underwriting process. This integrated approach offers a promising solution for streamlining insurance workflows while maintaining high levels of accuracy and efficiency.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Hybrid Model for ASD Detection Using Visual Features and Questionnaires
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition that requires early and precise diagnosis for effective intervention. Affecting 1-2% of children aged 2 to 14, traditional diagnostic methods rely on subjective clinical assessments, which can cause delays. This study proposes an AI-based multimodal framework combining facial image analysis and text-based evaluations using deep learning and machine learning. The VGG19 convolutional neural network extracts facial features, while a Random Forest model analyzes text-based data. When used separately, VGG19 achieves 60% accuracy, and Random Forest reaches 40%. However, by combining both models using weighted averaging (60% VGG19, 40% Random Forest), the predictive accuracy increases to 98%. Preprocessing steps like feature extraction, normalization, and statistical validation enhance the model's robustness. Additionally, interpretability analysis identifies key predictive features, further validating the system through p-value analysis. The results show that multimodal data fusion significantly improves diagnostic accuracy, making ASD detection more objective, scalable, and efficient. This research emphasizes AI's potential to revolutionize healthcare, enabling data-driven, accessible clinical decision-making for neurodevelopmental disorder diagnosis.

title: Early Autism Screening via Multimodal Flat Affect Recognition in Voice and Facial Cues
abstract: Flat affect, characterized by reduced facial and vocal emotional expressiveness, is one of the key indicators of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in children. The present article suggests a novel automatic system for the early identification of flat affect in 8–11 years old children using a multimodal fusion of facial movement, head pose, global attention, and voice-based emotion features such as pitch, volume, and speech patterns. A decision model integrates all these features to enhance the detection of emotional expressiveness deficits. Compared to previous research on a single modality, this multimodal approach increases detection reliability. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high performance with 90% accuracy, 92.86% precision, and 86.67% recall. The proposed system provides an effective, objective tool to assist in early ASD symptom detection and intervention for psychologists, educators, and parents.

title: Neo4j-powered graph-rag system for financial insights on the Colombo stock exchange
abstract: Financial annual reports contain rich but unstructured corporate information, making it difficult to efficiently extract relationships such as directors, subsidiaries, auditors, and ownership structures. Knowledge graphs provide a structured way to model these relationships and integrate heterogeneous information sources [1]. With recent advances in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), graphbased retrieval can be combined with large language models to improve factual accuracy and context grounding in downstream analysis [4]. In this work, we transform Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) annual reports into a Neo4j-based financial knowledge graph and integrate it with an LLM-driven Graph-RAG pipeline that supports naturallanguage financial querying. Our method introduces a focused retrieval strategy that extracts entities only from the most relevant text segments, overcoming LLM context limitations. This targeted approach enables near-complete entity capture and more accurate graph construction than full-document extraction.

title: Prediction of Meander Migration in Deduru Oya; A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Meandering is a natural occurrence in a sinuous river that is caused by erosion and sedimentation of banks. This can be predicted by various hydrological and mathematical methods. However, the application of remote sensing and machine learning to predict meander migration is yet to be explored. This study explores the possibility of using satellite imagery and machine learning approaches to predict meander migration in lower Deduru Oya. A numerical dataset was extracted using images to predict meander migration, and a TCN(Temporal Convolutional Network) was trained as the best approach, yielding MSE value of 0.30 and R Squared value of 0.59. The inferences of TCN were explained using saliency maps, visualizing feature, and timestep importance.

title: Convolutional neural network–based automated quality grading of cinnamon peel
abstract: Ceylon cinnamon, endemic to Sri Lanka, holds significant culinary, medicinal, and economic value, reinforcing the country’s position as the leading global exporter of authentic cinnamon. However, current processing techniques, particularly manual peeling and quill preparation, are highly labor dependent and introduce quality inconsistencies, limiting scalability. While national efforts increasingly promote value addition and product diversification, maintaining consistent export-grade quality remains challenging. Recent research highlights the potential of technological advancement within the cinnamon value chain, with image processing applied for maturity estimation, and diameter-based grading [1], [2]. Additionally, deep learning models, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have demonstrated strong performance in agricultural applications such as disease diagnosis and adulteration detection [3], [4]. Visual grading of cinnamon based on peel texture, surface defects and residual bark remains subjective and inconsistent. This study addresses this gap by proposing an objective, scalable deep learning–based automated visual inspection framework.

title: Automatic vehicle classification system for estimating traffic density
abstract: Traffic congestion is a common urban issue that increases passenger stress and leads to significant fuel waste due to prolonged waiting times at traffic junctions. Currently, traffic lights operate on preset timing systems that do not adjust based on real-time traffic conditions, failing to prioritize roads with higher vehicle density. To address this issue, in recent years researchers focused to prioritize the vehicle movement on each road based on real time vehicle density measurement. In this paper, we focused on popular pre trained models such as convolutional neural network (CNN), YOLOV8 algorithm, KNN, and MOG2 are selected to identify the traffic congestion through the video frames and images received by cameras. The experiment was carried out using the popular traffic areas in northern area dataset, which has 7000 image samples of different traffic roads with 7 classes of vehicles. The dataset is split into two subset such as training and testing. 6222 images were used for training and 778 images were used for testing the system. The detection component of the system includes the elimination of background and the retrieval of data to determine the number of vehicles spotted. The models performance was evaluated using classification accuracy, sensitivity and specificity. Based on this vehicle classification, traffic density is calculated. The experiments proved that DenseNet-121 achieved 98% higher classification accuracy, and 67.63% for MOG2, 88.64% for KNN, 96% for YOLOV8 and 97.3% for CNN.
